element: Airtable as the only edit point and source of truth
v1_location: EMST_Infrastructure_Setup_Guide Parts 0 and 5; v1 platform-architecture session
rationale: Project lead decided the repo is the single source of truth. Airtable sat on an EPIC subscription (free-plan scripting limits hit during setup), creating an owner dependency and no CI or provenance. An optional editing UI may remain only if it exports to the repo.

element: GitBook as the public publication layer
v1_location: Setup Guide Part 3; task sequence v7 Tasks 17-19
rationale: GitBook is a third-party dependency. Replace with a static site generated from tagged releases (CP Tier 1). Keep v1's three-tier visibility idea (core content, on-page tags, expandable workforce panel).

element: Release plan: v0.9 pre-Delphi tag, v1.0 post-Delphi R1, v1.1 R2, v2.0 annual
rationale: Keep tagged releases. Replace numbering and cadence with charter Art. 6: MAJOR no more than every 3 years with 12 months' notice; MINOR annually in a fixed month; PATCH as needed incl. quarterly crosswalk refresh; DOI per release; 24-month support window.

element: License: README states CC BY 4.0 while the repo was created with the CC0 dropdown
v1_location: Setup Guide Step 1.2 item 12; README draft
rationale: Contradictory signals that adopters' legal reviewers will notice. Adopt layered licensing: CC BY 4.0 content; CC0 schema, IDs, vocabularies and crosswalk tables; Apache-2.0 code; Tribal-related content excluded unless the Tribal Council authorizes. CP flagged the same contradiction.

element: Delphi validation (Tasks 20-21): panels per profession family; SAF, USFS and Tribal NR departments as priority partners
v1_location: task sequence v7 Tasks 20-21; README draft
rationale: Keep structured expert validation but redesign under IO. Recruit panels through consortium societies and design-partner agencies so validation also builds commitment, with COI controls. Tribal participation only through the Tribal Council/TN protocol, never as a default 'validation partner'.

element: Delphi reviewer access via view-only Airtable share
rationale: No consent, confidentiality or records controls. Use an IRB-reviewed survey instrument run by the host institution.

element: Sentinel network (Task 22): annual cycle; practitioner nodes via SAF, TWS, SER, AWRA, AEA, Tribal NR organizations; fire, permitting and WFIC channels
v1_location: Task 22 specification (task sequence v3 session); task sequence v7
rationale: A sound concept. Institutionalize under charter Art. 3.8 with paid honoraria, recruitment through consortium members and pilot organizations, and an annual cycle feeding the MINOR release. Tribal channels only via TN protocol.

A bus-factor risk federal adopters will see. Inconsistent with the validation, Tribal consent, quarterly crosswalk and adopter support v2 requires. Replace with a ~5 FTE steward and a published 3 FTE floor.

element: EPIC as implicit owner with long-term maintenance unresolved
v1_location: v1 private working record; Setup Guide footer
rationale: EPIC becomes the incubating steward through Dec 2027 (to be confirmed by the project lead) and permanent founding partner. A university host is chosen by open call, with an independent Consortium governing.

element: 'Community-governed' and 'field resource, not a proprietary product' claims
v1_location: v1 README and GitBook landing drafts
rationale: No governance body, change process or seats existed. The claim becomes true only when the charter is adopted and seats are filled.

element: Change Log (CL-NNN entries with rationale and open issues)
rationale: Good provenance practice. Migrate entries into the repo decisions log. Note that stale counts (215/6/43 vs 222/7/45) persisted in project instructions.

element: Inconsistent public competency counts (215 in v0.9 release text; 222 in database; 292 on GitBook landing draft)
v1_location: Setup Guide Step 1.5; GitBook landing draft; Change Log CL-014
rationale: Public counts must be generated from the release build, never hand-typed. Flag to DE and CA.

element: SAF as the most developed validation partner
rationale: SAF is active in 2026 with accreditation, Certified Forester and continuing education. Broaden to a multi-society consortium to avoid forestry skew and jurisdictional tilt.

element: Burning Glass Institute as a potential partner
rationale: BGI is active (Oct 2026) with its Skills-First initiative and AI tracking. Pursue BGI as a data and benchmark partner.

element: WFIC as named sentinel channel and proposed F16 Wildland Fire Intelligence
v1_location: task sequence v7 WFIC-1 to WFIC-3, Task 22
rationale: USWFS was established Jan 2026 and aligned fire qualifications take effect Jan 2027. Define by function (fire intelligence and decision support), link to NWCG rather than duplicate it, and use USWFS as the adoption route.

element: Five-platform architecture with Google Docs for governance memos and decision rationale
rationale: Decisions and governance records belong in the repo decisions log, where they keep provenance and stay public.
Keep only for one-off narratives built from tagged releases after a claims review, consistent with CP.
My understanding is that CEP is awarded by the Academy of Board Certified Environmental Professionals (ABCEP). Verify before any credential crosswalk.

element: Per-domain lists of professional associations and recommended credentials
rationale: Useful seeds for the credential crosswalk (LC, IA) and the ecosystem map. Each needs 2026 status verification.
Early demand-signal list (USAJOBS PDs, agency handbooks). Fold into IA ingestion. Several entries cite Wikipedia or commercial training vendors and are low quality.

element: Fire and permitting as priority context channels
v1_location: task sequence v7 Task 15.5 and Task 22
rationale: Both are live policy windows: USWFS qualification alignment, OPM series consolidation, CEQ permitting data standard.

element: Sector application notes limited to five sectors (Public Agencies, Private, NGOs, Consulting, Academia)
v1_location: Competencies source text; v1 baseline sector_applications
rationale: Federal-and-state-first adoption needs federal, state, local and Tribal distinctions. Align with CA's sector-actor variants; Tribal variants only on TN-protocol terms.

element: Airtable as the working database and single source of truth
rationale: Conflicts with the lead's decision that GitHub is the single source of truth. During v1 setup the free plan lacked scripting and CSV imports failed on narrative sheets. No validation between Airtable and GitHub; one editor is a single point of failure. CA reaches the same conclusion.

element: Manual CSV export and upload through the GitHub web UI
rationale: No schema validation, no build provenance, error-prone file replacement. Replace with CI that validates and builds from tagged releases (DE).

element: GitBook as the public, readable interface
rationale: A hosted third-party SaaS: third-party scripts and requests, limited control over accessibility conformance, weak support for computed data-driven views (role change, gap check, pathways). Docs, if needed, are generated in the same static build.

element: GitBook SUMMARY.md navigation by domain and skill area
rationale: Users arrive with a role, a person or a team, not a skill-area code. Make role the front door; keep domain and skill area as a facet.

element: Repository licence: CC0 selected in the GitHub dropdown while the README states CC BY 4.0
rationale: Two licences on one dataset make agency counsel hesitate. Choose one per artifact type (recommend CC0 data, Apache-2.0 code) and record it in release metadata; exclude third-party material.

element: 'Pre-Delphi, provisional pending expert validation' release language
rationale: The one place v1 disclosed uncertainty well. Generalize it into evidence tiers shown on every value in the UI and exports.

element: Delphi reviewer access by view-only Airtable share
rationale: Ties expert review to a proprietary workspace and cannot record attributed, dated assessments. Use structured review records in the repo (assessment records with rater type and date) and a non-GitHub route for agency staff.

element: Airtable view 'Delphi Priority - High Implicit Ethical'
rationale: It filters on L1-L5 ethical-lens columns that are unpopulated in V3, so it returns nothing. Ethical-lens disposition belongs to CA and LC; the product will surface lenses only after they are populated and reviewed.

element: Flourish Story as the public narrative channel
rationale: Third-party embeds, publicly published data, limited accessibility control, and claims that are hard to version against releases. Keep Flourish only for one-off advocacy pieces built from a tagged release after a claims review (AS).

element: Slide 1 subtitle 'Based on SAF-accredited competency standards, validated against OPM and O*NET classification systems'
rationale: Neither validation has occurred: Delphi has not run and there is no competency-level OPM or O*NET crosswalk. A false validation claim would cost credibility with exactly the federal audience the first job targets.

element: Slide 3 headline '38% of competencies remain Human-Essential'
rationale: Uses competency-level modal labels. Only about 21% of tasks are H. The modal hides the jaggedness the instrument exists to show. Single-analyst data presented as a headline percentage.

element: Slide 5 CLD numbers (High 9, Moderate 25, Low 15; 49 flagged)
rationale: Stale against the normalized baseline: 62 competencies are CLD-flagged, with severities including 'Highest' and 'Ungraded' that are outside the dictionary. Any public number must be generated from the current release.

element: Slide 5 annotation 'All CLD signals are concentrated at entry-level (P-position)'
rationale: Stated as a finding, but it comes from one analyst with no inter-rater reliability. CA proposes computing CLD at pathway level from role profiles. Show it as a hypothesis with its tier until it is re-derived.

element: Slide 8 headline '68% of competencies are in active transition'
rationale: The stability tier is fully determined by a rule (any reform flag or any Ac/S task), so it stores no independent judgment. CA retires the stored tier.

element: Slide 4 headline '58% of competencies carry policy reform sensitivity flags'
rationale: The reform flags are timeless booleans for dated, reversible federal events. Show policy change as dated driver events on the role-change view, not as a headline share.

element: Severity and exposure palette (green / amber / red-orange; red for High CLD)
rationale: Relies on hue, and the red-green contrast fails for common colour-vision deficiencies. Use a colour-vision-safe palette with patterns and direct text labels; never colour alone (USWDS guidance).

element: Headline discipline: 'every headline states the argument, not the chart'
rationale: Matches USWDS guidance to state the intended message as text, and it suits screen-reader users. Keep it, with the evidence tier inside the headline sentence.
Generalize to a release ID and DOI stamped on every page and export (records and defensibility).

element: Funder-first story architecture (scope, structure, disruption, risk, reach)
rationale: Serves the Proposal Evaluator, not the charter's first users (training leads, HR, workers). The product leads with a role; AS may keep a funder narrative for advocacy, generated from releases.

element: Forester PD transformation prototype ('Same Title, Different Job')
rationale: The clearest product expression of the vision: PD to competencies to exposure to redesigned role. It becomes View 1, generated from role-profile and assessment data rather than hand-authored (CA agrees).

element: Forester prototype: exposure shown as certain categorical labels (e.g. 'HUMAN-ESSENTIAL')
rationale: No tier, rater, date or agreement is shown. Add the uncertainty display standard (mvp_spec 7).

Self-contained HTML (good: no third-party requests) but 0 ARIA attributes or roles, layout-only grouping of the before/after panels, and no text alternative for the visual comparison. Rebuild to WCAG 2.2 AA.

element: Forester prototype: 'New Competency Requirements' and 'Career Pathway Redesign Implication' sections
rationale: These become the 'Emerging in this role' block and the pathway view, with CLD treated as a pathway-level computation.

element: v1 persona framework (Accreditation Aligner, Pipeline Defender, Team Architect, Infrastructure Builder, Curriculum Designer, Career Navigator, Proposal Evaluator, Sovereignty Practitioner; plus funder personas)
rationale: Good use contexts and a useful 'if the taxonomy doesn't X, this persona can't Y' framing. Never tested with users, and weighted toward funders and analysts. Merge with CM's personas; validate in Round 0; the Sovereignty Practitioner is defined only by TN and the nations.

element: v1 React drill-down explorer and SVG radial (sunburst) visualizations
rationale: Taxonomy-first navigation (domain to skill area to competency). The v1 author found the sunburst truncated labels and the explorer unattractive. Radial hierarchies are hard to make accessible and hard to read.

element: Display of competency-level modal exposure and CLD in UI layers
v1_location: Dimension Tags T13 modal columns as used by v1 visualizations
rationale: Display exposure at task level as attributed assessments, with role-level roll-up only as time-share bars carrying an evidence-mix line. CA retires the stored modal columns.

element: Exposure data provenance column (session-direct vs reconstructed or retrospective)
rationale: 147 session-direct vs 75 reconstructed or retrospective. This feeds the evidence-tier badge directly, so users can see which judgments were reconstructed.
CA retires the stored modal column, but the disagreement it records must survive as a 'contested' marker on the affected task assessments in the UI.

element: Maintenance model 'a single analyst position augmented by AI'
rationale: A real constraint the architecture must respect (static, low operations, no hosted services). It is not a stewardship plan: the domain, DOI, ACR and security packet need a named owner (AS).

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Spatial data models, coordinate reference systems, topology, spatial query/overlay logic, spatial data quality. Tool-bound: Operating a specific desktop GIS; print-map production workflows. Disposition: merge durable core with 2.1.4 into 'Analyze spatial data' ; GIS software to tools layer (DC-TOOL-001/002). Title names a tool category, not a capability; T1 layer creation is CLD-Moderate (AI layer generation).

Durable share High. Durable core: Radiometric/spectral/temporal resolution trade-offs, classification and change-detection logic, accuracy assessment with independent reference data. Tool-bound: Specific sensors and processing packages. Disposition: keep as durable competency; rewrite anchors around accuracy assessment; link DC-CAND-10 for foundation models. Durable; EO foundation models change the method, not the competency.

Durable share Low. Durable core: Positional accuracy, datums, error budgets, location metadata. Tool-bound: Device operation, vendor correction workflows. Disposition: fold durable core into field data capture (merged 2.3.3/2.3.4/4.1.5) and DC-CAND-03; devices to tools layer. Should be FC primary with DC secondary when collected in field; v1 DC primary over-assigns DC (Rule 3).

Durable share High. Durable core: Spatial statistics, autocorrelation, scale effects, suitability and connectivity modeling, spatial validation. Tool-bound: GIS toolboxes. Disposition: carry as 'Analyze spatial data' (absorbing 2.1.1 core and 2.7.5); observable anchors. Durable.

Durable share High. Durable core: Visual encoding, symbology, uncertainty depiction, audience-centered design. Tool-bound: Web-map platforms and template tools. Disposition: broaden to 'Design visual evidence', merge into DC-CAND-22 / DC-CAND-11. Durable; absorbs 2.7.4.

Durable share High. Durable core: Data modeling, normalization, integrity constraints, keys, retention and backup. Tool-bound: Specific DBMS products. Disposition: carry with observable anchors; CLD-High flag retained for formation design. Durable; relational concepts have >15-year half-life.

Durable share High. Durable core: Design-based vs model-based inference, assumptions, effect sizes, multiplicity, uncertainty. Tool-bound: Statistical packages. Disposition: carry; add uncertainty anchors (DC-CAND-11); absorbs 2.4.5 as specialization. Durable.

Durable share High. Durable core: QA/QC planning, data quality objectives, audits, error correction with audit trail. Tool-bound: QC software; AI anomaly detectors. Disposition: expand to include automated/AI QC (absorb 2.6.4) and link to DC-CAND-05 provenance. Durable core; automation shifts work from doing QC to designing and auditing QC.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Computational thinking, reproducibility, testing, code review (incl. AI-generated code), version control. Tool-bound: Specific languages, IDEs, libraries. Disposition: rewrite as DC-CAND-08 'Reproducible, auditable analysis'; languages to tools layer (DC-TOOL-023/024). Carries v1's CLD-High (T1) - formation pathway for debugging judgment is compressed by AI code generation.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Documenting fitness for use; vocabulary and standards conformance; judging metadata accuracy. Tool-bound: Metadata editors, templates (ISO/FGDC/Dublin Core named in text). Disposition: merge into DC-CAND-06 (stewardship & publication); standards to tools layer (DC-TOOL-029). Authoring being automated (USDA generative metadata pilot); work shifts to reviewing machine-generated metadata.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Measurement principles, calibration and drift, siting representativeness, network design. Tool-bound: Logger and IoT products. Disposition: split: field deployment & calibration (FC primary, DC sec; to FC's lane) vs DC-CAND-04 sensor-network data engineering. v1 DC primary hides the field judgment in siting and maintenance.

Durable share Low. Durable core: Survey design, photogrammetric principles (GSD, overlap), accuracy assessment. Tool-bound: Specific aircraft, flight apps, photogrammetry software. Disposition: merge with 4.5.4 (duplicate); flight operations FC primary; processing/accuracy into 2.1.2. Duplicate of 4.5.4 Drone/UAS operation; FAA rules are tools/policy layer.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Data-capture design (forms, validation at entry, sync integrity). Tool-bound: Tablets, ruggedized devices, apps. Disposition: merge 2.3.3 + 2.3.4 + 4.1.5 into one 'Design field data capture' competency (DC primary, FC sec). Three overlapping v1 competencies.

Durable share Low. Durable core: Little beyond 2.3.3 core. Tool-bound: iNaturalist, Survey123 named in tasks. Disposition: retire as stand-alone; residual into merged field data capture; apps to tools layer (DC-TOOL-015/016). Tool fluency by definition.

Durable share Low. Durable core: Field communication protocols for safety. Tool-bound: Radios, satellite phones. Disposition: move to FC/4.4 Safety & Emergency Response; equipment to tools layer. Not data craft; a safety competency.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Problem framing, train/validation/test separation, leakage, class imbalance, evaluation metrics, transfer and OOD, ground truth. Tool-bound: Frameworks and AutoML products. Disposition: rewrite around the ML lifecycle including pre-trained and foundation models; absorb 2.6.1, 2.6.2 (ML part), 2.6.3. Modality-specific AI competencies (vision, acoustic) will fragment as multimodal models spread.

Durable share High. Durable core: Model formulation, calibration, validation, sensitivity and uncertainty analysis, scenario design. Tool-bound: Modeling platforms. Disposition: carry; link DC-CAND-09 (fitness-for-purpose) and DC-CAND-12 (forecast systems). Durable; proficiency text generic.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Decision analysis, structured decision making, designing for real decision contexts. Tool-bound: Dashboards, DSS software. Disposition: rewrite as DC-CAND-22. Title is a system category.

Durable share High. Durable core: Graph methods for connectivity, spread, social networks. Tool-bound: Network libraries. Disposition: carry as specialist competency; consider merging into spatial analysis (connectivity) at CA's discretion. Durable but narrow.

Durable share High. Durable core: Trend, seasonality, autocorrelation, change-point and forecasting methods. Tool-bound: Packages. Disposition: merge as specialization under 2.2.2 statistical analysis (or keep) - decision for CA. Durable; overlap with 2.2.2 T2 and 2.6.3 T2.

Durable share Low. Durable core: Facilitation (belongs to SC/communication). Tool-bound: Video-conference platforms. Disposition: retire from data craft; facilitation in any medium to SC/Domain 5; platforms to tools layer. Not data craft.

Durable share Low. Durable core: Version control, records integrity, access control. Tool-bound: Cloud document platforms. Disposition: merge into records management (3.3.5) and DC-CAND-05 provenance. Tool category title.

Durable share Low. Durable core: None beyond 3.1.x project management. Tool-bound: Trello, Asana named in tasks. Disposition: retire; durable PM lives in 3.1.x; software to tools layer. Tool fluency by definition.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Knowledge capture, classification, retrieval design. Tool-bound: KM platforms. Disposition: rewrite as DC-CAND-18 'Curate authoritative knowledge corpora for retrieval-augmented AI'. RAG assistants make corpus curation consequential.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Process modeling, decision points, controls. Tool-bound: Workflow automation platforms. Disposition: merge into DC-CAND-14 (human-in-the-loop review design) and 3.x process design. Durable core is control design, not the platform.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Validation with ground truth (T3). Tool-bound: Model training frameworks; camera-trap AI products. Disposition: merge into rewritten 2.4.1; validation into DC-CAND-13; tools: MegaDetector, SpeciesNet, VIAME. Pre-trained detectors (MegaDetector adopted by Michigan DNR, TNC) shift work from training to validating.

element: 2.6.2 Acoustic monitoring and analysis with AI
rationale: Durable share Medium. Durable core: Acoustic survey design (FC), detection thresholds, validation, occupancy from detections. Tool-bound: BirdNET and similar. Disposition: split: deployment to FC; classification to rewritten 2.4.1; validation to DC-CAND-13; design to DC-CAND-03. Modality-specific.
Durable share Medium. Durable core: Forecasting and early-warning design. Tool-bound: ML platforms. Disposition: merge into 2.4.2 and DC-CAND-12. Duplicates 2.4.2/2.4.5.

element: 2.6.4 Automated data processing and quality control with AI
rationale: Durable share Medium. Durable core: Design and audit of automated QC. Tool-bound: AI QC tools. Disposition: merge into 2.2.3 and DC-CAND-04. Duplicates 2.2.3 with AI.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Interpretability methods and their limits; communicating model behavior. Tool-bound: XAI libraries. Disposition: merge into DC-CAND-09 and DC-CAND-11; T3 (accountability) into DC-CAND-19. Explanations of embeddings are limited ('not independently interpretable').

Durable share Low. Durable core: Little evidenced. Tool-bound: AR devices and engines. Disposition: retire to tools layer (watch); no deployment evidence in environmental inventories. Among 438 USDA/DOI/EPA use cases the only AR entry is a pre-deployment USDA Food Safety policy-review app; none in environmental field work (DC-001).

Durable share Low. Durable core: Instructional design (belongs to 5.4). Tool-bound: VR hardware/content tools. Disposition: retire from data craft; education design to 5.4; VR to tools layer. Not data craft.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Model-data fusion, assimilation, update and validation cycles, fitness for purpose. Tool-bound: Twin platforms, game engines. Disposition: rewrite as DC-CAND-12. Misfiled under immersive tech; NOAA evidence is forecast-system work.
Durable share Low. Durable core: Visual communication (see 2.1.5). Tool-bound: 3D/immersive platforms. Disposition: merge durable part into 2.1.5 / DC-CAND-22; platforms to tools layer. Tool fluency.

Durable share Medium. Durable core: Terrain/surface modeling from LiDAR/photogrammetry, vertical accuracy. Tool-bound: CAD/3D software. Disposition: merge into 2.1.4 / 2.1.2. Durable core is surface modeling.

element: 7.2.1 Validating AI outputs against ecological and regulatory ground truth
rationale: Durable share High. Durable core: Independent validation, error taxonomies, documentation of validation. Tool-bound: None named. Disposition: promote and rewrite as DC-CAND-13 (add sampling, observable products). Strongest data-craft competency in v1.

element: 7.2.3 Calibrating professional judgment in human-AI collaboration
rationale: Durable share High. Durable core: Reliability profiling, documented override decisions, bias self-audit. Tool-bound: None named. Disposition: carry with observable anchors; pair with DC-CAND-15 (organizational benchmarking). Durable; individual-level counterpart to DC-CAND-15.

Durable share High. Durable core: Adoption decisions, oversight architecture, monitoring of governance. Tool-bound: None named. Disposition: keep SC primary for authorization; add DC secondary; move technical risk tiering to DC-CAND-19 and HITL design to DC-CAND-14. v1 says DC secondary 'not warranted' (DC-045); evidence that designation hinges on substantive human review (DC-001) contradicts that.

element: Domain 2 skill-area structure (2.1-2.7 organized by technology family)
rationale: Seven skill areas are technology families (GIS, data management, field technology, analytics, collaboration tools, AI monitoring, immersive tech). About 9 of 35 competencies are almost pure tool fluency (2.3.4, 2.3.5, 2.5.1, 2.5.3, 2.7.1, 2.7.2, 2.7.4 retire; 2.1.3, 2.3.2 largely). Reorganize data craft by durable function along the information chain: Acquire (monitoring/measurement design, field data capture, sensor data engineering), Steward (data management, QC, provenance, publication, sensitive data), Analyze & Model (statistics, spatial, RS, ML/foundation models, process models, forecast systems), Integrate & Communicate (decision support, visual evidence, uncertainty, LLM text analysis), Assure & Govern (AI validation, HITL design, evaluation sets, model risk, procurement, enterprise governance). Tools move to a separate layer (tools_layer_proposal.csv).

Advanced/Expert statements are generic and unobservable across nearly all 35 competencies ('Shapes GIS strategy and standards', 'Provides leadership on ...', 'Expert in ...'). They cannot support hiring or assessment (IO's standard). Replace with scope-of-accountability anchors (own work -> own products -> systems others rely on -> organizational portfolio) and named work products; see datacraft_proficiency_anchors.csv.

element: Exposure codes for SA 2.6 in database vs working record
v1_location: v1:Dimension Tags T13 (2.6.1 T1-T2, 2.6.3 T2, 2.6.5 T2)
rationale: The SA 2.6 working record confirms Auto Type Ac for 2.6.1 T1 and T2 (and A,Ac,A sequences for 2.6.3 and 2.6.5) with Lo tacit/C career for 2.6.1 T1, but the database and normalized baseline record A/Hi/X for 2.6.1 T1 and A for the others (provenance 'Reconstructed (D2)'). DE/LM should reconcile before v2 carries any exposure value forward.

element: v1 Datacraft definition ('making patterns visible and projecting futures')
rationale: Pattern-making and projection are exactly what AI now produces cheaply. The irreducible human data-craft contribution is warrant: producing evidence whose provenance, method, uncertainty and fitness for a decision the practitioner can show and answer for, including when machines did the computation. Redefine accordingly (see report section 3).

v1 has 79 DC-primary and 91 DC-secondary tags (170 of 222). Rule 3 was right: Domain 1 science knowledge competencies (e.g., 1.1.1 Ecosystem dynamics, 1.1.3 Succession) are DC primary although their irreducible content is disciplinary knowledge used by all three crafts. Keep Rule 3 and add the knowledge-vs-craft distinction below.

element: DC-primary tags on Domain 1 science-knowledge competencies (26 of 40)
rationale: Disciplinary knowledge (ecology, hydrology, climate science, genetics) is the substrate for field, data and state craft alike. Tagging it DC primary inflates data craft and hides its dependence on field and institutional practice. Propose that v2 distinguish knowledge areas from craft practices (craft tags apply to practices; knowledge areas list which crafts draw on them). Decision for CA/IA.

element: Secondary-FC liberal rule for DC-primary competencies
rationale: Carry and strengthen: for any DC competency that validates or applies models/AI describing ecological condition (DC-CAND-09, -10, -13), FC secondary should be required, because out-of-distribution failures are recognized in the field first.

element: 3.4.3 Cryptocurrency, digital payments, and decentralized finance
rationale: Tool- and trend-bound; zero blockchain, cryptocurrency or distributed-ledger use cases among 438 USDA/DOI/EPA entries in the 2025 inventory; durable content (financial controls, donor transparency) is covered by 3.4.x and 6.6.x. Move blockchain/crypto to the tools layer as 'watch'.

Nearly every task specifies 'AI-powered', 'IoT', 'blockchain', 'RPA bots' or 'real-time dashboards'. This dates the competencies and makes them unassessable when tools change. Rewrite tasks by function (e.g., 'verify supply-chain material flows' not 'using blockchain and IoT'); move named technologies to the tools layer.

element: 6.7.2 T1 'Use environmental justice screening tools (EJSCREEN, CalEnviroScreen)'
rationale: Named public tools are volatile; my understanding is that EPA removed EJScreen from its website in early 2025 (expert recollection, not re-verified this session - LM/DB to confirm). Rewrite as 'apply cumulative-burden screening methods and evaluate the indicators and data behind them'; tools to tools layer.

element: 6.3.2 T2 'Use tools like InVEST or ARIES'
rationale: Tool names in task text; move to tools layer and state the durable method (ecosystem-service production-function modeling and validation).

element: 6.4.4 Public comment management (T2 classified S - substitution)
rationale: Deployed and piloted comment tools are documented as supplemental with analyst verification (FWS DocketScope; EPA Region 8 pilot; USDA pilot) and DOI's PCAT was retired between inventories (DC-001). Current evidence supports Ac/V (compressed, supervised), not S. LM owns exposure coding; DC recommends re-coding and linking to DC-CAND-16.

No USDA/DOI/EPA use case in the 2025 inventory reports AI as the principal basis for policy comparison or compliance determinations: EPA's high-impact cases prioritize inspections or pre-review documents, and the USDA permitting tool is explicitly 'recommendations for authorized staff to review'. S calls need direct evidence (LM lane).

element: F7 Environmental Data Science family Core list
rationale: F7 is Core for every Domain 2 competency, including virtual meetings, project management software and VR education. Re-derive F7 Core from the durable data-craft functions; retired tool competencies should not define a profession family.

Answer to v1's Delphi question: keep a Human-AI practice cluster, but as a cross-cutting 'Assure & Govern' function of data craft that also carries SC-secondary competencies; populate the never-drafted 7.2.4-7.2.5 with DC-CAND-16 and DC-CAND-17.

v1 has no competency every practitioner is expected to hold for using data and AI. Add DC-CAND-01 and DC-CAND-02 as Tier DC-1 universal competencies (assessed at Foundational for all, higher for some).

element: Data provenance, sensitive-data protection, model risk, AI procurement, evaluation sets (absent)
rationale: See DC-CAND-05, -07, -15, -19, -20. Each is evidenced in federal policy or deployments and missing from v1.
Merge; FC primary for flight operations and safety; DC secondary for processing and accuracy.

element: No persistent IRIs or machine-readable release

element: Airtable as the editing master (Airtable -> GitHub -> GitBook)
v1_location: v1 Infrastructure Setup Guide Parts 0 and 4-5
rationale: A proprietary SaaS base as the only editable source is single-vendor lock-in and loses row-level provenance at CSV export; it also contradicts the project lead's decision that GitHub is the single source of truth. Editing tools (Airtable, sheets, forms) may stay as clients that submit pull requests against repo data

element: Licence ambiguity (CC0 selected in GitHub; CC BY 4.0 stated in README)
v1_location: v1 Infrastructure Setup Guide Step 1.2 item 12

element: Three tasks per competency as the task layer
rationale: Too thin to be the NLP linking target or the CA task spine: linking plan text to individual v1 tasks scored P@1 0.43 (dev) / 0.39 (held-out) vs 0.53 / 0.48 for whole-competency documents. Carry tasks as seed L2 records with lineage, but expand and crosswalk them to O*NET task statements before using task-level linking

element: Rich competency text (tasks; proficiency; indicators) as linking evidence
rationale: Indexing the full v1 text beat title+description alone (dev P@1 0.53 vs 0.45; Hit@5 0.88 vs 0.80; held-out Hit@5 0.78 vs 0.65). Keep indicators and anchors in v2 records even before IO revision because they carry the vocabulary that links real-world text

element: Coverage gaps exposed by plan requirements
v1_location: Whole taxonomy (no home for these functions)
rationale: 14 of 72 non-noise gold items had only a weak v1 fit, all in seven functions: range/grazing management; recreation management (ROS; travel; capacity); scenery management; transportation/roads; minerals and energy authorizations (incl. oil and gas lease stipulations); lands and realty; wilderness stewardship. NMF clusters of 5994 low-similarity USFS components repeat the same themes (e.g. 641 range/livestock; 533 motorized recreation/ROS; 482 scenic/wild and scenic rivers; 419 roads; 391 minerals; 159 oil and gas stipulations). Route to DB/FC/SC as candidate competencies (see candidate_competencies.csv)

The five v1 sectors (Public Agencies, Private Sector, NGOs, Consulting, Academia) do not match the seven v2 sector actors (federal, state, local, Tribal, NGO, private, academic) and mix a business model (consulting) with sectors. Carry text as provisional enactments with alias refs (EMSTv1:sector/...) and re-derive

Useful as navigation views and as an interim grouping, but they should not be crosswalk anchors: roles (L3) carry OPM/SOC/state-class mappings. Give families persistent IDs (FAM) so views remain citable

Carry every v1 value as a dated, attributed ExposureAssessment record (instrument emst-v1-task13; v1ProvenanceCode session_direct/reconstructed) rather than as task properties, so later instruments (AEI shares, panels) sit beside it without overwriting
This is exactly the lineage the v2 provenance object needs; mapped to provenance.derivedFrom.v1ProvenanceCode in the example bundle
Agree with CA: move to dated DriverEvent records (jurisdiction; instrument; date; status) linked to tasks/roles; a boolean cannot be versioned or retired when a rule is stayed or rescinded

Keep v1 level names as aliases (EMSTv1level:*) so lineage survives, but anchor v2 proficiency to the L0 level-of-responsibility vocabulary once IO/CA decide DP-4; schema already references levels by ID, not by name
Dashboard counts stored as data go stale and diverge from tags (v1 data dictionary documents a 59-flag discrepancy between summary and per-competency counts). Compute at build time from records
Give each indicator a persistent ID so assessments and badges can align to it (OB3 Alignment to CFItem/ceasn:Competency); IO decides which are observable

element: Years-based proficiency level labels (Foundational 0-2 y; Intermediate 3-5 y; Advanced 6-10 y; Expert 10+ y)
v1_location: source text level labels (data/v1_baseline/source_text/proficiency.csv source_level_label); Proficiency Indicators sheet
rationale: Tenure is a weak predictor of performance (prehire experience rho ~ .06) and a known adverse-impact and age-claim exposure when used as a threshold. It duplicates and conflicts with OPM specialized-experience rules and the push toward technical assessments under the Chance to Compete Act and the Merit Hiring Plan. It also disadvantages cross-sector movers with discontinuous careers. v1 own methodology research recommended responsibility-based levels instead. Replace with L1-L5 responsibility-anchored levels; keep years only as descriptive typical_time_to_level from survey data.

element: Four levels applied to every competency
rationale: Forces levels where no such work exists (e.g., 2.5.2 Collaborative document management has an Expert level "Advances document management in environmental sector"). Adopt per-competency level spans defined only where job analysis, SME consensus and assessable indicators support them (proficiency_model_v2.md s.5).

v1_location: Proficiency Indicators col Knowledge; Competencies sheet
rationale: 85.5% scored 0 or 1 on OBS-4 in the blind sample (61% inferred states such as Understands/Familiar/Expert in; 24% reputation, e.g., Shapes). 209/222 Foundational K begin Understands/Familiar/Aware; 217/222 Advanced K begin "Expert in"; 211/222 Expert K begin "Shapes". Rewrite as testable knowledge elements (layer B), not performance statements. UGESP content validity cannot rest on inferred mental states.

Only 16% directly observable; 61% need specification; 23% not individually assessable (mostly Expert: "Provides leadership", "Leads transformative"). Fold into L-level indicators with condition and standard.

v1_location: Proficiency Indicators cols Indicator 1-6, levels FOUNDATIONAL and INTERMEDIATE
rationale: The best v1 measurement content: 56% (F) and 42% (I) directly observable; 88% of sampled competency-levels contain at least one direct non-proxy statement. Carry as raw material for L1-L2 indicators, adding conditions, standards and evidence metadata per indicator_writing_rules.md.
Only 15% directly observable and 69% need specification; 21% opportunity-dependent (lead programs, manage portfolios); 17% compound. Rewrite to L3/L4 with explicit complexity and scope conditions.

61.4% not individually assessable; 22% proxies (publishes, recognized); 39% opportunity-dependent; on average 81% of each competency Expert statements match a few boilerplate frames. Only 1 of 43 sampled competencies has a direct non-proxy Expert statement. Do not migrate. Write new L4/L5 indicators only where the work exists.

element: Publication, recognition and award indicators ("Publishes influential research", "Achieves recognition", "Recognized expert")
v1_location: Proficiency Indicators, mainly EXPERT (publishes in 158 competencies; recognition in 103)
rationale: Criterion-contaminated proxies that favor academic and well-resourced roles and are scored by others opinions; unusable for selection in agencies; adverse-impact and opportunity-access risk. A published method may serve as an evidence source for a performance indicator, never as the indicator.

element: Credential and training completion as indicators (e.g., 4.4.4 "Completes OSHA HAZWOPER Technician (40-hour) training")
rationale: Credentials are qualification gates attached to positions, not levels of competence. 4.4.4 also appears to pair emergency-response levels (Awareness, Operations, Technician) with site-worker course hours (24 h, 40 h), which IO judges a content error (FC/CP to verify against 29 CFR 1910.120).

element: Tool- and vendor-named indicators (ArcGIS, QuickBooks, Workiva, FARSITE, Tableau, blockchain, digital twin as the competency)
rationale: 5.8% of sampled statements tool-locked (9% at Advanced); 17.9% of job tasks name AI or a specific technology. Move tools to the separately versioned tool layer and name the function in the indicator (DC lane).

Verb-led (good) and close to O*NET task style, but: only 7.5% state a standard or protocol; 31% are compound; 8% lead with "Use" (tool-as-task); three tasks per competency is far too few for job analysis; tasks were written top-down from competencies rather than derived from jobs; about 76% of D3 task text was inferred (task sequence v7). Carry as seed items for the job-analysis survey task inventory, to be confirmed by incumbent ratings.

element: Claim that T1-T3 run from foundational to advanced
rationale: Not supported by v1 own tags: only 89 of 222 T1 tasks are tagged primary-learning (P); 170 of 222 T3 tasks are tagged contributing (C), only 11 specialist (X). Task position does not encode proficiency; level must come from the indicator model.

Parse defect in all database versions: K/A sit in the Indicator 1-2 columns with "Knowledge*:" and "Application*:" prefixes; Indicator 3 is the placeholder "Indicators*:"; zero real indicators for 30 competencies. The source text holds 706 D5 indicators. Recover them (DE), then rewrite to v2 rules. D5 scored lowest in the sample (6% direct, 50% usable) because only K/A could be rated.

element: Indicator truncation at import (6 per level cap)
rationale: 2,104 of 6,484 source-text indicators (32%) are absent from the database, including all 706 D5 indicators. Recover before rewriting so v2 does not lose usable observable content (DE lane).

element: Competency descriptions merged into titles (19 competencies, e.g., 1.4.2, 3.1.4, 4.3.3)
v1_location: Competencies sheet Description blank; title holds description
rationale: Data defect (DE). Matters for measurement because SMEs rate titles and definitions in Delphi and surveys; merged text confuses item stimuli.

element: Near-duplicate competencies (1.4.2 Wildlife survey techniques vs 4.1.2 Wildlife observation and sign interpretation)
rationale: Identical Foundational Application text ("Conducts wildlife surveys following (established) protocols") and overlapping indicators. Duplicates undermine discriminant validity and double-count in profiles. Merge or separate on a defined boundary (e.g., field detection vs survey design); CA to run a systematic near-duplicate screen.

element: AI/robotics exposure instrument (5 dimensions on 666 tasks: automation type, tacit density, career-ladder position, vector, horizon)
v1_location: Dimension Tags T13 columns; data/v1_baseline/tasks.csv; domain4_task12_working_record.md
rationale: Concept sound and task-level grain correct, but codes come from a single analyst with an LLM, with no inter-rater reliability. v1 explicitly decided IRR provisions were not needed. The only repeated coding is same-rater version drift on D6 (auto type 95%, tacit 93%, career 89% agreement), which is consistency, not reliability. "Calibration" in v1 meant tuning the instrument to the analyst judgment. Run the s.7 gold-set study before any exposure statistic is published as more than analyst judgment.

element: Career Ladder Destruction (CLD) flag and severity
v1_location: Dimension Tags T13: CLD Flag, CLD Severity
rationale: Deterministic rule (TRUE if any P-position Ac/S/V task) is violated in 11/222 competencies (5%): 7 D2 reconstructed rows should be TRUE, 3 D4 rows should be FALSE, and 4.1.3 should be TRUE. Severity uses out-of-dictionary values ("Highest", "Ungraded"); flags mix True/False/Yes/No/Y/N. Make CLD computed rather than stored (CA s.4) and validate inputs; keep the construct, which is important.

Single-rater irreducibility judgments; v1 own record lists many contested boundary cases (2.3.2 drone, LCA producer vs consumer, 7.2.3). Reliability unknown at competency or task level. Run the craft-weight pilot (validation_protocol.md s.7.3) before DP-5.
Single-rater; S1 holds 107 of 215 primary tags and S6 only 3, which may reflect coder convention rather than work. Test with the s.7.1 gold set and SME review; CA may generalize to work functions.

v1_location: Dimension Tags F1-F15; Profession Family View
rationale: Analyst-assigned importance. Replace with empirical importance and frequency from the job-analysis survey (validation_protocol.md s.4) aggregated by role profile; keep v1 values as priors only.

E/I/A coding is highly inferential (v1 reports ~95% of ethical content Implicit), so reliability is likely low without a strong codebook; transposed L2/L3 numbering across working documents adds error risk. If retained, run the s.7.1 reliability test before population; otherwise express ethics through observable indicators (e.g., 7.1.3 exemplar).
Derived rule applied consistently (0 violations against reform flags and Ac/S tasks), but it inherits the unvalidated inputs. Carry as a computed field once inputs are validated.

element: Planned Delphi design (~30 panelists; 3-5 reviewers per competency; Tasks 20-21)
v1_location: taxonomy_task_sequence_v7.md (Tasks 20-21); Delphi panel-composition prompt in project conversation record (~30 panelists, 3-5 reviewers per competency)
rationale: With 5 reviewers per item, CVR significance requires 5/5 essential; with 3 it is unattainable. No pre-registered thresholds, stopping rules or composition caps; SAF-led recruitment risks forestry skew. Replace with 15-25 per panel, pre-registered rules, CREDES/ACCORD reporting and contraction-bias correction (validation_protocol.md s.3, s.5).

element: Sentinel network: single analyst with AI coding, no IRR
v1_location: Infrastructure architecture decision conversation (2026-03-03); Structural Conditions report
rationale: Keep the sentinel idea (an annual leading indicator) but replace single-analyst coding with the s.7.2 LLM-plus-human protocol and composition caps. v1 itself identified the failure mode (AI resolves ambiguity silently) and the composition risk (contraction over-represents private datacraft practitioners).
Useful descriptive context; not assessable and should not be used in selection. Carry as context examples; CA may restructure as sector-actor variants.

Most observable Foundational and Intermediate content in v1 (D7 sample: 40% direct), with explicit validation behaviors that suit assisted-mode assessment. Expert levels repeat the boilerplate and must be rewritten. 7.1.3 integrity needs care in selection use (SJT and work products only; never trait scoring).

element: Hard-coded regulatory references in tasks and indicators (e.g., SEC climate disclosure in 3.6.2 T2; "NEPA scientific integrity requirements" in 7.1.3)
rationale: Rules change (2025 shifts in SEC climate disclosure and NEPA implementation, as IO understands them; unverified, SC/PS to confirm). Standards in indicators should reference applicable jurisdiction requirements via a jurisdiction overlay (jurisdiction_variable flag).

element: v1 methodology recommendation of SFIA-style responsibility levels and level spans
v1_location: Skills Taxonomy Architecture and Methodology...md (Proficiency scaling comparisons)
rationale: v1 own research recommended a responsibility-first architecture that avoids forcing every skill into every level for mobility and career-pathway products. v2 adopts it (proficiency_model_v2.md).

element: Domain 5 stakeholder framing listing Tribes as a stakeholder category (5.2.1 source text Foundational indicator)
rationale: Tribal nations engage as sovereign governments through consultation, not as stakeholders. Exemplar rewrite adds an indicator distinguishing the two; TN to review.

v1_location: Dimension Tags: T13 Tx Auto Type
rationale: One code mixes three constructs: technical exposure, deployment mode (who executes) and staffing outcome. In the pilot, v1 'A' covers both LLM-augmented desk tasks and tool-assisted physical tasks (6 of 9 matched A tasks are physical; 3 of 9 are E0). Split into exposure-by-vector, deployment mode and role-level outcome

Keep the idea; tighten the definition. Its measurable core equals Eloundou E1 (task time cut by at least half at equal quality): 11 of 13 matched Ac tasks are E1/E2 and 10 of 13 sit at T2-T4 on the GPT-4 automation rubric. Move 'headcount compression plausible' to a role/organization outcome that depends on demand, budget and policy (Bessen; Humlum and Vestergaard)

v1_location: T13 Auto Type = S (4 in database; 9 in synthesis)
rationale: All 4 database S tasks are rated exposed (E1/E2), but none at T4 (full automation) on the GPT-4 rubric; federal inventory shows NEPA/permitting AI at pilot/pre-deployment (0 deployed) and public-comment tools at pilot. Present S only where deployment is registered and directive usage is high. The synthesis-database discrepancy (9 vs 4) must be reconciled

v1_location: T13 Auto Type = V; R4, R10
rationale: The A/V current-deployment rule matches the AEI distinction between directive (system executes) and collaborative modes and Microsoft's 'AI action' vs 'user goal'. Re-anchor examples to registered deployments

Separate descriptive 'no current technical pathway' from normative 'should remain human' (accountability). Of 10 matched H tasks, 7 are E0 but 3 are E2 (e.g., land-use dispute mediation): the work is LLM-exposed in capability terms even where authority must stay human. Domain 7 all-H is normative (agrees with CA)

element: FC/DC structural pattern ('H only in FC/SC primary')
rationale: Circular (R1 told coders to expect it; FC and H share criteria) and contradicted by the data: the database holds 9 H tasks on DC-primary competencies, not the 1 anomaly claimed. Re-test only with blind coding

Near-deterministic with auto type in v1 (no Hi-tacit Ac/S/V) - a coder-inference signature. Externally, tacit density is predictive but not determinative (Lo: 17 of 19 matched tasks exposed; Hi: 5 of 11 exposed). Rate independently (SME panel; O*NET experience/job-zone and work-context descriptors) before linking to exposure

Derive from role profiles (grade band, job zone, FWD grade distribution), not assert per task. P tasks in the pilot are more often E0 (9 of 22) than C tasks (4 of 20) because entry work is physical; ladder risk concentrates in desk entry tasks

Add a sensing/remote-observation vector (field observation replaced by sensors, imagery, eDNA, acoustic monitoring) - the dominant environment-specific vector, measured by no index; calibrate Ro against the Sep 2026 robot task index and Webb robots

Replace with dated assessments plus deployment-stage evidence (OMB inventory stages; adoption shares). Horizon 3 is never used; N fuses 'no horizon' with H; all Ac are Horizon 1 and all H are N (collinear)

v1_location: T13 CLD Flag, CLD Severity; R9
rationale: Keep the concept (strongly supported by canaries evidence in private payroll). Compute at pathway level and attribute drivers: the observed 2025-26 public-sector ladder damage is fiscal/policy (hiring freeze, seasonal halt, senior exits), not AI. Add a 'top-of-ladder loss' mechanism. Fix vocabulary drift (Yes/True; 'Highest', 'Ungraded' not in dictionary)
Convert to a watchlist with explicit external triggers (e.g., matched AEI tasks show high directive share and success; deployment registered in inventory; posting volumes fall)
Compute from dated signals rather than store; current rule mixes reform flags and exposure into one label

Code/title errors verified against BLS matrix: 19-1012 is Food Scientists and Technologists (Farm and Home Management Educators is 25-9021); 33-1021 is First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers, not Fire Inspectors; 29-9021 (Health Information Technologists) and 25-4031 (Library Technicians) are poor fits. O*NET-SOC details exist for several 'no SOC' families (13-1199.05, 11-1011.03, 19-2041.01-.03, 15-1299.02, 19-2099.01, 19-1031.02/.03). Rebuild at O*NET-SOC 8-digit, many-to-many, with OPM series
666 tasks in database vs 645 in synthesis; S 4 vs 9; H 146 vs 136; Ac 101 vs 92. Treat the database as authoritative and archive synthesis counts as superseded
Correct instinct; extend to rater type, codebook version and date for every assessment
Static counts; recompute from the change-signal layer

Add attributed external assessments per task (Eloundou labels, AEI task penetration/directive share, Microsoft IWA metrics, physical flag), with crosswalk match type and confidence; show agreement with v1 analyst labels

63.4% (563/888) begin with non-observable leads (Understands 173, Expert in 190, Shapes 189). Usable only after rewrite to observable verbs with conditions; Foundational and Advanced/Expert rows are the problem, Intermediate ('Applies...') is mostly fine.
99% begin with an action verb (Supports, Conducts, Designs, Leads...). Usable as one-line level summaries for learners and as the spine of competency-level outcomes, once Expert rows are revised.

Mostly observable seeds (Apply-band verbs ~37-38% of rows). Good raw material for learning outcomes; only 5.8% of all indicators state a criterion or standard and only 25 state supervision/independence, so each needs condition and criterion added. IO owns assessment-readiness.
Many read as position duties ('Leads...', 'Develops agency procedures') rather than demonstrable outcomes; usable for role profiles and capstones, not as course outcomes.

158 of the 192 competencies with parsed expert indicators (82%) include a 'Publishes...' indicator; 'Influences', 'Recognized' also common. Academic-reputation bias excludes practitioners who reach expert standing through agency or field leadership; Expert should be recognized through evidence (portfolio/peer review), not taught.

Tenure bands contradict competency-based design (a reskilling learner can reach Intermediate in months). Define levels by autonomy, complexity, scope and responsibility for others; keep years as a typical-time note only.

Knowledge/Application text is misparsed into indicator cells for all 30 D5 competencies, so D5 has no usable indicators. The misparsed text is actually well written (autonomy cues such as 'with supervision', 'Independently'); repair, do not discard (DE).

Best-written v1 content for learning use: observable indicators with conditions, explicit escalation and documentation behaviors. Use as the writing model for v2 outcomes and as the core of the AI/data-literacy baseline pathway (LC-PW-06).

element: 7.2.2 Designing workflows for tacit knowledge formation
rationale: This is the supervisor/learning-designer competency that operationalizes CLD response (formation tasks, by-hand quotas). Elevate it as a required competency for supervisors and training officers.
Real tasks (CA audit) and the natural unit for work samples, task books and simulations. T1-T3 roughly track level but are not level-tagged; add an explicit typical-level field per task.

element: Task 13 exposure tags (auto type, tacit density, career-ladder position)
rationale: Directly usable to set work-based-learning share and by-hand quotas (template rules R6-R7). Must carry attribution and await IO inter-rater reliability before driving funded programs.
CA finds the tier is fully rule-determined. For learning use, replace with computed change velocity plus lifecycle status to set credential currency (refresh intervals).
Mean 6.2 words; too thin to write authentic cases. Expand into short scenario prompts per sector actor (context for assessment items and case teaching).

element: Labor Market Crosswalk F10 primary SOC 19-1012
rationale: Code/title mismatch: 19-1012 is Food Scientists and Technologists in SOC 2018; Farm and Home Management Educators is 25-9021. Soil and Plant Scientists (19-1013) is the better primary.

element: Labor Market Crosswalk F12 primary SOC 33-1021
rationale: 33-1021 is First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers, not Fire Inspectors. Wildland roles map to 33-2011, 33-2022, 45-4011, 19-4071 and supervisors to 33-1021.

element: Labor Market Crosswalk F13 primary SOC 29-9021
rationale: Health information occupation is the wrong concept; environmental health maps to 19-2041 and 19-4042, occupational health to 19-5011.

element: Labor Market Crosswalk F11 secondary SOC 25-4031
rationale: Library Technicians is a poor fit; nonformal educators map weakly to 19-1031 (park naturalists) and 25-3021; formal to 25-2031.
