element: Family-level SOC crosswalk as the only program link
rationale: Programs and accreditors need CIP-SOC-role-competency links, not family-SOC. Replace with a versioned CIP-SOC-EMST crosswalk (starter: cip_soc_env_crosswalk.csv) and, later, role-level links.

CEQ's NEPA regulations were removed (final rule 2026-01-08); agencies now follow their own procedures (e.g., USDA 7 CFR 1b final 2026-04-03; DOI handbook 2026-02-24). Re-anchor to 'applicable agency NEPA procedures' and move named rules to a dated context layer.
Scoped to public EE. v2 also needs workforce-learning competencies (qualification design, field evaluation, mentoring) for training officers and supervisors; see LC-C-01, LC-C-02.
SAF Forestry C4-A.1/A.2 and Forest Technology C4-A.1/A.2 require identification of regionally important trees and use of keys; v1 has no such competency (LC-C-03).

element: Forest operations, wood products, scaling and certification
rationale: Required by SAF Forestry C4-C.4/C4-D.5 and Forest Technology C4-C.5-C.6/C4-D.5-D.8; route to DB/FC for subsector module.

element: Environmental-health operational content (epidemiology, food protection, vector-borne and zoonotic disease)
rationale: EHAC methodology and List 1 require these; v1 has zero hits. Route to DB for an environmental-health module (LC-C-07).

element: Water/wastewater treatment operations and OT cybersecurity
rationale: ABET ETAC and EHAC List 1 include treatment/unit processes; water operators are a large state/local workforce; v1 has no treatment-operations competency and cybersecurity appears in one indicator (LC-C-05, LC-C-06).
SAF requires compass/pacing orienteering without battery-powered units; add as a foundational indicator of 2.1.3 or a field-navigation competency.

element: Workplace evaluator / qualification-system and prior-learning content
rationale: Zero v1 hits for task book, evaluator or prior learning, yet performance-based evidence depends on evaluator capacity (LC-C-01).

element: Indicators that are credentials or course completions
v1_location: about 27 indicators, mostly D4 (e.g., 4.2.3 F I1 S-130/S-190; 4.2.3 I I1 RXB2; 2.3.2 and 4.5.4 F I1 FAA Part 107; 4.4.4 HAZWOPER; 4.4.2 WFR/EMT; 4.5.3 CDL; 4.7.2 ISA)
rationale: These record inputs (training taken, credential held), not observable behavior. Move them to the evidence-equivalence register (P-LC-07) as recognition evidence for the competency-level, and replace them with behavioral indicators. Also check the 4.4.4 hour/level pairings: v1 appears to mix HAZWOPER site-worker training hours with emergency-response levels (verify against 29 CFR 1910.120).

element: 6.7.2 and 7.1.3 indicators naming date-sensitive tools or rules
v1_location: 6.7.2 F I2 (EJSCREEN, CalEnviroScreen, CEJST); 7.1.3 I I1 (NEPA scientific integrity requirements)
rationale: Named screening tools and rule-specific requirements change faster than the competency; move names to the tools/standards layer with dates (CA R-4). Current availability of federal EJ screening tools was not verified this session.
Every accreditor reviewed (SAF C4-7, GCSE IES, ABET SO) treats systems reasoning as an outcome; decide whether it is a transversal competency (CA DP-3).

element: Profession families (F1-F15) as the unit of mobility analysis
v1_location: Dimension Tags F1-F15; Profession Family View; profession_family_definitions.md
rationale: Families are disciplinary identities, not jobs or sector-actor contexts, so family similarity cannot answer the charter's question (movement between federal, state, local, Tribal, NGO, private and academic). The CM computation finds a two-island structure: a biophysical/field-science cluster (F1-F7, F10, F12) and a statecraft/human-systems cluster (F8, F9, F11, F13-F15) with ZERO pairs above chance between them (33 above-chance pairs, all within clusters; partition identical in 150/150 Louvain runs). Keep families as navigation groupings of role profiles (agrees with CA); compute mobility on role profiles with sector-actor variants

element: Core tag definition ('a meaningful gap'; boundary tests for distinctiveness)
rationale: For mobility use, Core encodes what is DISTINCTIVE to a professional identity, so Core-only similarity systematically understates transferability by design. Core-only rankings correlate only 0.51 (Spearman) with Core+Supporting rankings. v2 role profiles need importance and level per task, not distinctiveness, so overlap measures reflect what the job actually requires

Supporting tags carry most of the transferability signal (structure is stable at Supporting weight 0.25-0.75, Spearman >=0.99) but were assigned by one analyst with an LLM and no reliability check. Do not migrate as role requirements; use only as a prior to be re-elicited with importance ratings

v1_location: Dimension Tags Zero Core; Foundational Professional Prep
rationale: The idea is right and matters for mobility: 3.1.1-3.1.3 (project planning, budget, risk) are Core in no family yet Supporting in 10, the broadest portable foundation in v1. Re-express as a computed breadth/portability score on role profiles (agrees with CA's 'compute, don't store'). Note that 2 of the 3 carry CLD flags

The seven D7 competencies are the top 7 bridges (54% of 'cross-community core bridges'). Carry them into the transversal layer, but do not cite their bridging as evidence of portability: they were tagged across many families by design (Feb 2026), so the bridging is partly constructed

v1_location: Competencies: Public Agencies | Private Sector | NGOs | Consulting | Academia
rationale: Agrees with CA (retire structure, keep as seed text). Mobility-specific addition: all 1,110 cells are populated, so every competency claims to apply in every sector. The notes carry zero discriminating information for transferability and cannot be used to compute sector-actor similarity

element: CLD (career-ladder destruction) flag and R9 severity
v1_location: Dimension Tags T13 CLD Flag / CLD Severity; CLD Signal Register
rationale: Carry the concept and compute it per pathway (agrees with CA). Mobility linkage v1 did not draw: CLD concentrates where portability is highest. 37% of SC-primary competencies are flagged vs 20-22% FC/DC; 50% of 'broad foundation' competencies; 36% of the top-25 bridges vs 28% overall. Entry tasks that teach the most portable skills are the most compressed, so CLD is also a mobility risk indicator

Needed for entry and progression links on role profiles and for pathway-level CLD (metric M-19). Extend it with sector-actor variants, because entry ladders differ by actor (federal seasonal; corps; consulting junior; state trainee)

element: Craft primary/secondary as the representation of 'blends'
v1_location: Dimension Tags Craft Primary / Craft Secondary
rationale: Agrees with CA (blend profile, not classification). Computation shows blends are asymmetric. Field-management families (F1-F4, F10, F12) have even blends (evenness 0.91-0.99; e.g. Forestry FC 38/DC 38/SC 24) while statecraft-cluster families hold almost no field craft (FC 0.7-7%). The charter's 'blend of three crafts' describes field professionals, not policy, ESG, finance or education professionals in v1's tags

Agrees with CA. Mobility-specific point: validating family similarity against observed occupational flows (CPS, LEHD) needs correct SOC targets; with 7 of 15 mappings rated Low by v1 itself, flow-based validation is infeasible for half the families until role-level SOC/OPM-series/state-class crosswalks exist

element: Five Functional Positions framework (bridging competencies between information-flow positions)
rationale: A useful within-organisation mobility lens (Sensing <-> Structuring <-> Analyzing <-> Integrating <-> Deciding) that v1 never connected to its tags. Carry as a candidate work-function facet for role profiles (CA's L0) and test whether position adjacency predicts internal moves

It counts taxonomy outputs (craft distribution, Core counts, reform flags), not workforce outcomes. Replace with outcome and leading-indicator metrics (metrics_framework.csv) so the tool is held to outcomes, not deliverables

element: Fire Management <-> Land Use Planning tags
v1_location: Dimension Tags F9/F12; profession_family_definitions.md overlap notes
rationale: The family definitions name Fire <-> Planning overlap (community wildfire protection planning), yet Fire holds 0 of Land Use Planning's 13 Core competencies and similarity is below chance (z = -1.65). Either the tags omit real overlap or the overlap is in tasks v1 never wrote. Re-check in L2 with fire and planning SMEs; this is a high-demand pathway for displaced fire staff
Agrees with CA (redesign under IO). Add reserved Workforce Voice seats with ratings reported by stratum, and a usefulness veto at G1 (practitioner_panel_design.md)

element: Absence of any observed career-path data
rationale: v1 never tested a transferability claim against an observed move. Add consented career histories (panel), state HR prior-employment fields, OPM Federal Workforce Data and licensed career-history data as the validation layer for pathway claims (metric M-03)

Useful as seed illustrations of private contexts, but only 4 of 222 notes name a role and 0 name a credential, employer type, pay or hiring term, so they cannot support translation or mobility. Keep as provenance-tagged seeds; replace with private role-profile variants linked to private_job_frameworks rows.

Consulting is a delivery model, not a sector: consultants work for agencies (third-party NEPA contractors), companies and NGOs. 38 of 222 notes mention clients/billing/proposals - the only place v1 touches business practice. Model delivery_model (in-house | contracted | independent third-party) as an attribute of role variants, separate from sector actor. Agrees with CA audit section 7 and adds the delivery-model facet.
Undocumented marker on all four non-academia sector notes for 66 competencies; meaning unknown (possibly inferred text). DE/CA should resolve before any note is reused.

element: F14 Corporate Sustainability & ESG (family definition and 14 Core tags)
rationale: Definition is sound but anchored on strategy, materiality and narrative. 2026 evidence shows the function moving toward compliance-grade GHG accounting, controls and assurance under legal/finance (ESG controllers; 58% raising compliance priority; 63% cutting external comms). Re-center on disclosure, controls and assurance; split product/EPR compliance and EHS out.

Keep as a function, but its Core set duplicates itself (see 6.6/6.8/6.3/3.4 rows) and omits the private roles that dominate hiring: verification, integrity rating, dMRV, mitigation banking operations. Rename 'Environmental Markets & Conservation Finance'.

element: Private sector encoded as F14/F15 only
rationale: F14/F15 fall in the SC-dominant policy community in CM's analysis, which implies 'private = statecraft'. In fact the largest private environmental employment is technical FC/DC work: consulting plus architectural/engineering services employ ~34% of environmental scientists and specialists (27,410 of 80,730), more than state government (21,760). Private context must attach to every function, not to two families.

In-house EHS and compliance is a large private employer (and also public facilities) with distinct credentials (CHMM, CSP, CIH, CPEA) and no v1 home. Add as a work function and role group; source competencies PS-C10, PS-C24, rewritten 6.1.2.

element: Missing family/function: Environmental Assessment, Permitting & Mitigation (applicant and agency side)
rationale: Environmental review, permitting and mitigation is the core consulting product and the mirror of agency review work; v1 scatters it across 6.1, 6.6.2 and 1.x. A function-defined group with agency and applicant variants is the highest-traffic public-private bridge (TR-01, TR-06, TR-17). Coordinate with SC.
Tasks are tool-trendy (AI materiality, IoT, blockchain verification). Rewrite around durable strategy work (targets, governance, capital allocation) and move tools to the tools layer.

element: 3.6.2 Sustainability reporting and disclosure (GRI, SASB, TCFD)
rationale: Title and tasks cite TCFD (now folded into ISSB) and SEC climate disclosure (never effective; rescission proposed May 2026). No internal-controls or assurance content, which is now the hiring core. Rewrite to regime-neutral disclosure plus PS-C05 and PS-C09; put regimes (ISSB, ESRS, CA SB 253) in L4.
Substantially duplicates 5.2.1-5.2.5; merge into the engagement competencies with a corporate enactment note (investor, supplier, community).
Distinguish financial materiality (ISSB) from double materiality (ESRS, simplified top-down approach in revised ESRS 2026). Remove real-time sentiment-analysis tasks.

Description merged into title (data defect). Content overlaps 3.1.5; refocus on metric definition, data controls and linkage to compensation (38% of managers+ report ESG-linked bonuses - low-quality source).

Framed as voluntary strategy with blockchain/digital-passport tasks; private hiring increasingly follows compliance with producer-responsibility and chemical reporting laws. Add PS-C17; 3.7.4 description merged into title (data defect). DB owns subsector depth.
Carry the core but split corporate inventories (PS-C09) from project quantification and verification (PS-C06, PS-C07); these are different private jobs with different credentials.
Rewrite around the mature US compensatory mitigation and conservation banking market (PS-C14); treat biodiversity credits as an emerging extension.
Three overlapping competencies (transactions; carbon markets and trading; carbon credit and offset programs). Merge into one transaction/compliance-market competency plus PS-C08 integrity.

element: 6.6.5 Green bonds and sustainable investment vs 6.8.2 Green bonds and climate bonds
rationale: Duplicates. Retire 6.8.2 into 6.6.5 (keep provenance alias). Low US environmental-employer hiring traffic; mainly finance-sector roles.
Three overlapping competencies on conservation finance and market-based mechanisms; merge into one with land-transaction and blended-finance tasks.
Valid, but mostly international-development and NGO work with low US private hiring traffic; keep as a lower-priority module item.
High private relevance; tasks reference TCFD. Rewrite to IFRS S2-aligned scenario analysis (PS-C21); SB 261 enjoined, >45 jurisdictions on ISSB path.

element: 3.4.3 Cryptocurrency, digital payments and decentralized finance
rationale: No private environmental employer hiring signal found or known to this role; tool-trendy. Retire to the tools layer if kept at all.
Generic. Add billable-delivery content (estimate-at-completion, utilization, change orders, subcontractor management, invoicing) via PS-C03, with public enactment (COR, grants).
Assessment-only; private EHS jobs run compliance through management systems and certifying-official accountability (PS-C10).
Mixes agency-side review with applicant-side strategy; split into enactments or add PS-C11 so both sides of the most common public-private move are visible.
Carry; add contractor/applicant enactment (document preparation under agency direction, disclosure of interests) and update for 2025 procedural changes (SC lane).
Awareness-level; HAZWOPER-level site safety is the entry gate for consulting field work (PS-C24).
Highly relevant to private practice (applicant-prepared documents, verification independence, staff moving between sectors). Extend per PS-C18.

element: 7.2.1 Validating AI outputs against ecological and regulatory ground truth
rationale: Maps directly to consulting QA/QC and stamp/signatory liability; specialize per PS-C20.

Maps to catch-all SOCs. O*NET-SOC has more specific codes for sustainability work (e.g., sustainability specialists and chief sustainability officers under 13-1199 and 11-1011); IA/FH to verify exact codes. 19-2041 and 17-2081 should anchor consulting and EHS roles; 29-9011 for occupational health and safety.

element: Structural Conditions claim: O*NET 'Sustainability Specialists' employment 1,205,700
v1_location: Structural Conditions doc, Corporate Sustainability row
rationale: The figure appears to be the broad 13-1199 'Business Operations Specialists, All Other' group, not sustainability specialists; do not carry forward as a workforce-size estimate.

element: Structural Conditions claim: private 'market-premium niches' drain agency staff
rationale: Partly contradicted for technical roles: May 2025 BLS medians for environmental scientists show federal $116,110 vs consulting $79,320 and engineering services $83,500. Premiums exist in oil & gas and utility industries and in senior corporate sustainability roles, not in consulting science roles. Medians are compositional, so this is not a like-for-like comparison.

element: v1 proficiency bands (Foundational 0-2 / Intermediate 3-5 / Advanced 6-10 / Expert 10+)
rationale: Private ladders are defined by responsibility (task -> project -> program/client -> practice/revenue), not years; the seller-doer step has no v1 level. Supports a level-of-responsibility scale (CA DP-4).

element: Public Agencies sector note (one note per competency)
rationale: Merges federal, state, local and Tribal employers. Of 222 notes, 13 match a state term and 10 a local term; 167 name no level of government. Agrees with CA audit section 7: replace with sector-actor role variants and enactment notes.

All six are federal (NEPA timeline, CatEx, One Federal Decision, etc.). State drivers are absent: state environmental policy act amendments, delegation or assumption changes (e.g. Section 404), skills-based hiring orders, federal grant cuts to state programs. Replace with dated, jurisdiction-tagged driver events.

Defined from the proponent side ('securing regulatory authorization for management activities'). State and local permit writers, inspectors and enforcers are the other side of S3 and have no stage for compliance assurance and enforcement. Add regulator-side functions (authorize, inspect, enforce) to the work-function facet.

Do not fit continuous public service operations (water and wastewater plants, environmental health inspection programs, air monitoring networks). Add 'operate' and 'oversee delegated programs' functions. Agrees with CA audit section 8.
Split into (a) regulatory inspection by the authority (SL-C03) and (b) compliance management inside a regulated entity (PS lane). The task bundles and authority differ.
Rewrite as two role-variant enactments: permit writer (regulator, SL-C02) vs permit preparer (applicant/consultant).
Generalize to environmental review under federal, state and Tribal environmental review acts (SL-C08); keep NEPA as an enactment. States staff MEPA and CEQA units.
Keep and deepen: add the case arc from referral to settlement or litigation and expert testimony (SL-C04).
One competency covers monitoring, SIPs, permitting and enforcement. Split at least monitoring/testing (SL-C13) from planning and permitting; route to an air module.
One of few v1 competencies native to local government (MS4). Carry as the seed of a water-utility module.
Valid for state supervisors. Add labor-agreement administration and grievance indicators (MN PCS Principal spec).
Add intergovernmental instruments (cooperative agreements, Good Neighbor agreements, IPA assignments, delegation agreements, grant work plans).
Reframes a hierarchy as coordination. Add program oversight and delegation tasks (SL-C01, SL-C11).
Valid across state and local; link to the mobility instruments in mobility_map.csv.

element: Missing: water/wastewater operations; environmental public health services; solid waste facility regulation; oil and gas regulation; remediation fund administration; environmental financial assistance
rationale: Zero v1 text mentions these functions, yet the sampled state and local classes are full of them (TX Sanitarian, MI lead and copper, PA oil and gas, FL solid waste, MI MUSTA). Add as modules or core competencies (SL-C05 to C15). Agrees with CA audit section 6.

element: F13 Environmental Health & Justice to SOC 29-9021
rationale: 29-9021 is Health Information Technologists, a poor fit. Environmental health specialists are usually coded with environmental scientists and specialists, including health (19-2041), with SOC 2018 to be verified by FH/IA. State Sanitarian classes are a separate crosswalk target.
25-4031 is Library Technicians, a poor fit. FH/IA to propose a replacement; at state level interpretive and education roles sit in park ranger and naturalist classes (e.g. TX Park Ranger).

element: Family-to-SOC crosswalk as the only occupational join
rationale: States hire on classes, not SOC. Add a versioned state-class crosswalk layer (minimal_common_fields.csv) alongside SOC and OPM.

State ladders use years plus autonomy and supervision (TX I-V; WA 1-6; MI 9/10/P11/12), and years are substitutable. Crosswalk on supervisory status and autonomy as well as years; years alone mis-map across systems.

element: Sector application text as illustration seeds
rationale: Some Public Agencies notes are usable seeds for state enactment notes (e.g. 4.7.3 'Municipal stormwater utilities, MS4 programs'), but most are generic. Keep with provenance only where a state or local variant is confirmed.

element: Statecraft craft definition ('institutional navigation, policy, stakeholder engagement, and governance'; irreducible value 'enabling decisions across competing interests')
rationale: Keep the irreducibility test and the 'translates technical capacity into authorized action' idea. Sharpen the defining deliverable to a commitment that holds (authorized, legitimate, resourced, durable) and name nine teachable components (P-SC-01). 'Stakeholder engagement' is a means, not the deliverable; listing it as definitional is part of why statecraft became a residual category.

element: Statecraft as residual category: SC Primary on 94/222 competencies (42%), including 3.3.3 Facilities operations, 3.3.2 Equipment and asset management, 3.1.1 Project scheduling, 5.5.1 Visitor information, 5.4.3 Volunteer program management
rationale: These produce internal organizational outputs, not authorized commitments across institutional boundaries. Re-test D3 and D5 with the sharpened test: does the deliverable require authority, legitimacy or agreement from another institution or the public? Expect roughly 15-25 to move to 'SC secondary' or to a non-craft general-practice layer (CA decision). Otherwise statecraft looks inflated and loses diagnostic power.

element: Six reform-sensitivity flags as boolean columns (NEPA Timeline, Digital Permitting, CatEx Scope, Consultation, One Federal Decision, S2-S3 Boundary)
rationale: They sit on 129 of 222 competencies (184 instances in the v1 database), so they barely discriminate. They are also tied to the 2024-early-2025 reform agenda and are already stale: CEQ regulations are gone, Seven County changed review scope, and Sec. 112 fees, ESA rule changes, WOTUS, disclosure regimes and partnership authorities are not represented. Replace with a dated policy-instrument layer plus durable mechanism codes (P-SC-02); keep v1 flags as a frozen historical view.

Names an executive policy rather than a mechanism. The durable elements (one document, lead agency, joint schedules) are now in statute (NEPA sec. 107 as amended in 2023; FAST-41). Replace with mechanism 'multi-agency-coordination'. That EO 13807 was revoked in 2021 is from prior knowledge, not verified this session.

This describes the workflow model, not a reform. Its uses (13 in the Task 10 record, 10 of them in D6; 16 in the database) mix two mechanisms: concurrent review and handoff of instruments that span both stages. Move it to a workflow note and stop counting it as reform exposure.
Generalize to mechanism 'review-timeline' (statutory deadlines, Sec. 112 paid acceleration, state shot clocks, objection windows). Link to the dated instruments PI-NEPA-01/08 and PI-FOR-02.
Generalize to mechanism 'screening-exemption' (CE lists, CE adoption across agencies, CE for land management plans under USDA-38d, statutory CEs proposed in FOFA and SPEED, CEQA exemptions).

It conflates three different things: ESA sec. 7 process rules (2025-26 rulemaking), NHPA sec. 106, and sovereignty-based government-to-government consultation. Tribal consultation is a legal obligation owed to governments, not a 'reform' target. Split into 'esa-consultation', 'historic-preservation-review' and a non-reform 'sovereign-consultation' relationship tag (TN to own).

Keep as mechanism 'digital-process' but link it to dated instruments (PM 2025-04-15, CEQ standard v1.2, ePermit Act if enacted, PermitAI). It is the most used flag (66 competencies in the v1 database; the Task 10 record says 39, so the stored counts disagree) and the one most likely to persist.

Add 'judicial-review' (Seven County, SPEED standing and remedy changes), 'review-scope' (effects narrowing), 'jurisdiction-scope' (WOTUS), 'substantive-protection-change' (ESA harm, endangerment finding), 'authority-delegation' (state 404 assumption reversion; GNA), 'disclosure-requirement' (CA, EU, SEC), 'fiscal-mechanism' (Sec. 112 fees; GNA revenue retention), 'participation-requirement' (discretionary public involvement).

A tier that labels almost everything Transition does not discriminate. Derive stability from the instrument layer instead: competencies whose sensitive instruments changed status in the last 24 months, weighted by mechanism.

element: S1-S6 workflow model as the universal cycle
rationale: It is built on a project-based land-management cycle with NEPA as the paradigm for S2. It fits poorly for regulatory programs (permit issuance, renewal, inspection, enforcement: 6.1.5 Enforcement had to be tagged S2), water utilities (capital planning, rate cases, SDWA compliance), air districts (SIP planning, rulemaking, Title V), and corporate compliance (materiality, disclosure, assurance). Keep the stages as functions, add 'Make rules/policy' and 'Assure compliance and enforce', and define subsector workflow profiles (P-SC-03).

element: Stage 2 definition ('paradigmatic processes are NEPA analysis ...')
rationale: Generalize to 'Impact review' covering NEPA under agency procedures, state EPAs (CEQA, SEPA), Tribal review codes and voluntary or corporate impact assessment. Drop references to CEQ-regulatory constructs (e.g., cumulative effects as a required category) that no longer bind federally.

element: Stage 3 tagging rule naming 'One Federal Decision frameworks'
rationale: Replace with 'lead/cooperating agency and joint-schedule coordination (NEPA sec. 107, FAST-41)'.

element: 6.1.3 Permitting procedures (single competency for all permitting)
rationale: Too coarse. A Section 404 permit, an NPDES permit, a Title V permit, an ESA incidental take permit and a county land-use permit need different authority knowledge, but they share a durable core. Rewrite as a durable 'authorization pathway' competency (SC-C01/SC-C03) plus instrument-specific modules in the instrument layer. A March 2026 v1 permitting conversation found the same lack of permit-type granularity.

Rewrite. Job Task 2 'in accordance with NEPA regulations' is obsolete (no CEQ regulations since 2025-04-11). The competency now centers on picking the level of review under agency-specific procedures, page and time limits, documenting CEs and extraordinary circumstances, evaluating applicant-prepared documents, the Sec. 112 fee pathway, discretionary engagement and a defensible record. See SC-C02, SC-C03, SC-C04, SC-C06.

element: 6.4.4 Public comment management: T2 'Analyze comment themes' classified S (substitution) with entry-path elimination
rationale: Reclassify to Ac (compressive augmentation). AI comment tools are in production (CommentNEPA), but agencies must still respond to substantive comments, and SPEED would tie standing to 'substantive and unique' comments. That makes validating AI triage a record-integrity task. The entry path changes rather than disappears, provided it is redesigned (SC-C05).

element: All four v1 'S' (substitution) calls are on statecraft entry tasks: 6.1.1 T2 legal comparison, 6.1.2 T2 compliance checklists, 6.4.1 T1 policy literature review, 6.4.4 T2 comment theme analysis
rationale: This is v1's most important unremarked statecraft finding. The codifiable tasks juniors used to learn the law are the ones being automated. Add a craft-level 'apprenticeship at risk' signal and pair each exposed entry task with a designed developmental substitute (P-SC-06).

element: Task 13 claim that relational-institutional legitimacy competencies show 'no trajectory toward S or V in any domain'
rationale: True for the relational core (5.2.4, 6.5.1 T1-T2, 5.2.3), but 6.4.5 T1 (V), 5.5.2 T1/T3 (V) and 6.7.2 T1 (V) already sit inside statecraft competencies. The claim should be scoped to tasks, not competencies, and tested against real deployments (EngageNEPA, CommentNEPA).

Broaden to 'Legislative, appropriations and governing-body processes' across Congress, state legislatures, Tribal councils, county boards and utility commissions. Appropriations is missing from v1 (see 3.1.2).

element: 3.1.2 Budget development and management (project budgeting only)
rationale: Split. Keep project budgeting as management. Add a public fiscal and appropriations competency (SC-C10): budget formulation and justification, operating under continuing resolutions, cost recovery and fees (Sec. 112), revenue retention under agreements (GNA through FY2028) and grant compliance. The UK Policy Profession Standards treat Finance as a core policy standard.

Carry, with TN owning content. Distinguish a government's duty to consult (federal, state) from a Tribal government's own external-relations and regulatory roles, which v1 does not describe from the Tribal side.

Add cooperating-agency practice under new procedures (bureaus may deny requests with documented reasons), delegated and assumed program oversight and reversion (Florida 404), and county participation as cooperating agencies (SPEED would expand this).

Make instrument design explicit: GNA master and project agreements, recreation GNAs, co-stewardship agreements, MOUs, revenue retention and limits on inherent government functions. In FY2025 the Forest Service held 540 GNAs with states, counties and Tribes.

element: 6.7.2 Environmental justice screening and assessment (T1 names EJSCREEN, CalEnviroScreen)
rationale: Make it tool-agnostic and venue-aware. DOI's final NEPA procedures removed EJ references, so federal NEPA demand has fallen while state cumulative-impact regimes may persist (not verified this session). Reports that EJSCREEN was taken offline in 2025 are from prior knowledge and unverified. Keep EJ as the L1 lens; DB/SL to verify state laws.

element: v1 D6 Section 9 assumption that 'EJ requirements become embedded in regulatory frameworks at federal and state levels'
rationale: Outdated at the federal level (see 6.7.2). Restate as contingent and venue-specific.

element: 6.1.5 Enforcement procedures tagged S2 (Environmental Review) primary
rationale: Enforcement is post-authorization compliance assurance, not impact review. That it was tagged S2 is evidence of the workflow gap (see S1-S6 row).

Under USDA's 2026 procedures, plan amendments and revisions can be categorically excluded (USDA-38d-USFS), and the 2026 objection rule shortens windows. Planning statecraft moves from EIS production to component drafting, objection resolution and monitoring commitments. Update tasks.

Carry. These are the relational core (mostly H). Add an engagement-design competency for when participation is discretionary (SC-C06). Replace generic proficiency text with observable anchors (statecraft_proficiency_anchors.csv).
The V calls are plausible for transactional recreation and research permits. Keep the competency, but treat it as the digital-permitting operations entry point that feeds SC-C03.
Carry and extend to AI provenance in the administrative record and to disclosing AI assistance in documents (SC-C02, SC-C05).

element: Generic proficiency statements in D6 (e.g., 'Manages permit applications independently'; Expert 'Shapes NEPA policy and practice')
rationale: Not observable or assessable. Replace with behaviorally anchored indicators tied to work products (see statecraft_proficiency_anchors.csv). Note that the UK standards have the same weakness ('Understands', 'Champions'), so a national precedent does not by itself solve assessability.

element: Five sector application notes (Public Agencies, Private Sector, NGOs, Consulting, Academia)
rationale: There is no Tribal or local-government column, and 'Public Agencies' merges federal, state and local authority contexts that differ sharply. Replace with an authority-context tag (P-SC-04) and the sector-actor profiles in report.md.

element: Duplicate or overlapping finance competencies (6.6.5 Green bonds and sustainable investment vs 6.8.2 Green bonds and climate bonds; 6.6.4 vs 6.8.1 vs 3.4.2)
rationale: Probable duplication. Ask DB/PS to consolidate; it inflates SC counts.

element: 6.7.5 Air quality management placed under Environmental Health and Justice
rationale: Air-district work (SIPs, Title V and NSR permitting, rulemaking, enforcement, litigation such as Bay Area AQMD v. EPA) is a regulatory program, not mainly an EJ topic. DB should restructure it.

element: Scenario axes: federal investment level x AI adoption mode
v1_location: Structural Conditions of Environmental Management Professions.md, 'Workforce futures under alternative scenarios'
rationale: Investment is the wrong variable: FY26 funding fell only 1.9% while EPA (-24%), USFS (-13% net) and NRCS (-24%) staffing fell, so money and capacity decoupled. The axis is also federal-centric despite devolution. Adoption mode is a strategy choice, not an exogenous uncertainty, so it cannot be wind-tunnelled while it sits on an axis. Replace with capacity (rebuilt and coordinated vs thin and fragmented) x AI reliability and legitimacy (trusted vs brittle).

element: Scenario content: ladder destruction, crafts as reproduction regimes, refugia, ~2028 decision window, austerity bias in validation
v1_location: Structural Conditions report, Scenarios A-D and Taxonomy Implications
rationale: Strengthened by 2025-26 evidence: departing EPA staff median tenure 30.3 years; internships -43.8%; NOAA disaster database moved to an NGO refugium. Carried into SC1-SC4 and the no-regret moves.

v1_location: Structural Conditions report (all four quadrants assume AI works; only the adoption mode varies)
rationale: Add SC2 Human Premium and SC4 Patchwork Retreat. Evidence of failure-prone agentic projects, EO model degradation off-distribution, and unresolved legal acceptance makes AI brittleness a live future.
Scenarios without signposts cannot guide workforce decisions. Add the signpost dashboard (scenarios.md s8.5) and wildcards W1-W7, and feed them into L5.

element: Exposure = technical overlap x adoption mode x ladder fragility
v1_location: Structural Conditions report, scenario Taxonomy Implications
rationale: Concur with CA (add). Refine: keep technical exposure scenario-invariant (LM lane). Record adoption mode as the strategy under which an impact assessment is made, and make realized impact and reproduction risk scenario-conditioned (SC1-SC4) only for tasks above an exposure or CLD threshold.

Concur with CA: rule-determined, so it adds no information. Also internally inconsistent: the Workforce Signals dashboard reports 110/90/15 over 215 competencies, while the per-competency tags show 150/53/19 over 222. Replace with lifecycle state plus computed scenario robustness class (robust/contingent/fragile) and a protect flag.

element: Emergent tier and Domain 7 future-addition protocol (max 5 competencies per skill area)
v1_location: Data Dictionary: Stability Tier; Domain 7 Architecture Decision
rationale: Emergence needs a watch layer outside the core count and outside per-area caps; otherwise emerging content is either excluded or crowds out established content. Use lifecycle states watch -> proposed -> emerging -> established with evidence thresholds and review-by dates.

Concur with CA: horizon 3 is never used and N conflates two meanings. Replace with dated horizon bands (now/1-3y/3-5y/5-10y/10y+) on attributed L5 assessments, each with a review-by date, optionally scenario-conditioned.

v1_location: Dimension Tags.T13 S-Trajectory Flag; task13_crossdomain_synthesis s5.2
rationale: A good watch mechanism. Convert each flag into a watch item with named signposts. For example, 1.6.2 eDNA is watched against national strategy implementation; 2.2.4 scripting against agentic coding adoption in agencies.

v1_location: Dimension Tags.T13 CLD Flag / CLD Severity
rationale: Central to the no-regret moves (NR-1, NR-2) and the stress test, and corroborated in direction by entry-path data. Still needs evidence: single-analyst, and severity vocabulary is inconsistent in D6 ('Highest', 'Ungraded', Yes/No vs TRUE/FALSE). IO and LM to validate.

element: Sentinel Network (Task 22): fire, permitting and WFIC channels; annual survey; last in sequence
rationale: Carry the concept and channels. Change: start at v2.0, not after Delphi; add continuous intake, monthly scans, quarterly triage and event triggers; expand channels to all subsectors and actors; stratified, compensated sentinels to correct the austerity bias v1 predicted; a shared signal-coding schema feeding L5.

Replace static flags with dated policy-event signals linked to driver IDs (D-P02 SPEED Act/Seven County; D-P03 oscillation; D-P04 devolution; D-P07 state disclosure). Flags written before Seven County and CEQ rule rescission are already stale.

element: Profession families F1-F15 (+ proposed F16 WFIC) as the vehicle for emerging work
v1_location: Dimension Tags F1-F15; task sequence v7 WFIC-1..3
rationale: New work should enter as L3 role profiles with lifecycle status, not as new families. Families are slow and federal-centric; emerging roles (fire intelligence analyst, AI-assisted review lead, dMRV verifier) cut across families. Resolve F16 within the role layer.

element: 2.7.2 Virtual reality environmental education; 2.7.1 AR field applications; 2.7.4 immersive visualization
rationale: Tagged Emergent with no demand evidence found in this scan. Move to the watch layer with a 12-month review; retain 2.7.3 digital twin (expand to stewardship, FS-C11).

element: 3.4.3 Cryptocurrency, digital payments, and decentralized finance
rationale: No environmental-workforce demand signal found; tool- and fad-bound. Demote to watch (lapsing) or withdraw; keep any durable element (digital payments to landowners/participants) inside conservation finance competencies.

Keep, as policy and land-use scenario analysis. Add a distinct strategic-foresight competency (FS-C15: horizon scanning, scenario planning, backcasting for organizational and workforce strategy) so that foresight is assessable separately.
A durable ecological-futures competency, robust across scenarios; link to FS-C15 and to digital-twin validation under nonstationarity.

element: 7.2.1 Validating AI outputs; 7.2.2 Designing workflows for tacit knowledge formation
rationale: Expand rather than retire. 7.2.1 becomes the cross-family no-regret competency FS-C01 (plus FS-C02 model risk). 7.2.2 becomes FS-C13 (AI-augmented apprenticeship design). Both are robust in the stress test.

element: 3.6.2 Sustainability reporting and disclosure (GRI, SASB, TCFD)
rationale: Framework names belong in the tool and standard layer (L4). Disclosure regimes have shifted (Omnibus I scope cut; revised ESRS; SB 253 first reports Nov 2026). Rewrite around the durable function of assurance-ready disclosure across regimes (FS-C18).

element: Tribal NRM and co-stewardship coverage (6.5.1 Tribal consultation; 7.1.1 Indigenous data sovereignty)
rationale: Consultation-only framing understates the governmental roles Tribes are asserting (19 of 38 Roadless submissions sought authority beyond consultation). Agreement lifecycle craft (FS-C14) is needed. Content decisions go through TN protocol and real consultation.

element: Sector application fields (Public Agencies / Private / NGOs / Consulting / Academia)
v1_location: Competencies sheet cols S-W; all 222 competencies
rationale: 'Public Agencies' absorbs Tribal governments, so Tribal nations never appear as employers or sovereign regulators. Retire the 5-field structure (concur with CA) and add 'tribal' as a sector actor with sub-types (federally recognized Tribe; inter-Tribal organization/consortium; Tribal college; Tribal enterprise; ANCSA corporation; Native Hawaiian organization - distinct legal status; state-recognized Tribe - distinct status). Seed text stays as illustration only.

element: Domain 1 cross-sector line 'Tribal Nations: Traditional Ecological Knowledge integration, co-management science, cultural resource protection'
rationale: Reduces Tribal governments to suppliers of TEK. Tribal programs run multi-media environmental, forestry, fire, fisheries and water programs (GAP core capacities; CWA 106; CAA 103/105; 1,394 Tribal forestry employees in 2019). Describe Tribal employers by function, as for any government.

Co-locates Tribal government relations and Indigenous knowledge with DEI (5.3.4) and EJ (5.3.5). Tribal status is political/governmental, not demographic; in 2025-26 that placement has had practical consequences (agency-by-agency DEI exemptions). Move Tribal government-to-government content to Statecraft/intergovernmental; keep cross-cultural communication separately.

Proficiency fields empty in database; source text levels ('Comprehensive cultural expertise'; 'Leads organizational cultural transformation') are neither observable nor appropriate. Reframe as cultural humility with observable behaviors (asks about and follows protocols set by the host community; corrects own errors). Move 'Tribal consultation' sector note to 6.5.1.

element: 5.3.2 Indigenous knowledge integration (competency as a whole)
rationale: Competency-izes Indigenous knowledge itself and frames the goal as 'integration' into agency approaches. Replace with TN-C10 (engage with Indigenous knowledge only on holders' terms) and TN-C07 (Indigenous data governance) - competencies about the non-Tribal professional's conduct, not about the knowledge. DOI 301 DM 7 directs reliance on Indigenous Peoples to interpret their own IK and FPIC before receiving it.

element: 5.3.2 proficiency: Advanced 'Deep understanding of TEK systems'; Expert 'Recognized expert in TEK integration'
rationale: The project would be certifying non-Indigenous practitioners as experts in other peoples' knowledge systems. Authority over IK rests with its holders (301 DM 7 s.7.5, 7.6.A(5)). Not the project's to define.

element: 5.3.2 indicator 'Recognizes complementarity of TEK and Western science'
rationale: Presupposes the relationship between knowledge systems and asks the practitioner to assert it. Whether and how a nation's knowledge relates to agency science is that nation's call.

element: 5.3.2 indicator 'Documents Indigenous knowledge appropriately (with permission)' and Consulting note 'TEK documentation (with consent)'
rationale: Documenting IK should not appear as a default professional service line. Recording culturally sensitive information occurs only at a Tribe's request under its agreement and control of the record (NPS will not record culturally sensitive information without Tribal permission). Rewrite as 'records only what the knowledge holder authorizes, in the form and location the Tribe specifies'.

element: 5.3.2 indicator 'Ensures Indigenous knowledge holders are compensated and credited'
rationale: Keep and strengthen: compensation for time and services; compensation does not transfer ownership; credit in the form the holder chooses (including anonymity). Fold into TN-C10.

element: 5.3.2 T3 'Cite and acknowledge Indigenous contributions in planning documents' (exposure A)
v1_location: Tasks 5.3.2:T3; Dimension Tags T13 T3 Auto Type=A
rationale: Attribution terms are set by contributors; treat as H and bar AI drafting over Tribal-provided content unless the Tribe authorizes it. Exposure instrument needs a 'governed data' rule (see P-TN-09).

element: 5.3.3 T1 'Conduct field surveys to identify historic or sacred sites'
rationale: Non-Tribal surveyors can identify potential cultural resources and refer; determination of religious and cultural significance rests with Tribes (Tribal special-expertise language in current Section 106 rules, which the July 2026 draft would delete). Rewrite: 'Identify potential cultural resources and refer significance determinations to the THPO/Tribe'.

element: 5.3.3 T2 'Document and map cultural features using approved protocols' (exposure Ac)
rationale: Site-location data are confidential under NHPA s.304 and ARPA and plans carry explicit confidentiality standards (e.g., Mt Baker-Snoqualmie 1990; Umatilla 1990). Compressive AI augmentation of mapping invites uploading confidential locations to third-party AI. Add confidentiality indicator and flag task as governed-data in exposure layer.

Appropriate content for anyone working with Tribal nations; carry forward but rewrite substantially as TN-C02 (government-to-government consultation) plus TN-C01 (trust responsibility and treaty rights), TN-C04 (agreements) and TN-C05 (Tribal jurisdiction). Current levels are generic tenure bands ('Expert in tribal relations').

element: 6.5.1 indicators 'Incorporates traditional ecological knowledge appropriately' (Intermediate) and 'Integrates traditional knowledge with western science' (Advanced)
rationale: Consultation competency should not carry an IK-integration expectation. Replace with 'Requests or receives Indigenous knowledge only with free, prior and informed consent and on the Tribe's terms, and discloses records-law limits before receipt' (301 DM 7).

element: 6.5.1 Expert indicator 'Advances tribal capacity and leadership in environmental management'
rationale: Paternalistic framing: Tribes build their own capacity. What federal/state staff control is the barrier side. Replace with 'Removes administrative barriers to Tribal self-governance (timely payment and reimbursement, compactable funding, reduced reporting burden)', which Tribes asked for in 2025 consultation.

element: 6.5.1 T3 'Document and incorporate tribal input into environmental and land use plans' (exposure A; vector AI; horizon 1)
v1_location: Tasks 6.5.1:T3; domain6_task13 rationale 'AI assists documentation drafting'
rationale: Consultation records can contain information shared in confidence. Using third-party AI to draft from them is a data-governance decision for the Tribe, not a productivity default. Keep A only where the Tribe has agreed; otherwise H. Add standing rule (P-TN-09).

element: 6.5.1 T1/T2 exposure H via ARM (accountability relationship mechanism)
rationale: Sound reasoning: government-to-government engagement carries legal and political accountability that cannot be delegated to automated systems.
Replace with 'Tribal governance, federal Indian law and Tribally directed research partnerships under Tribal research codes'.

element: Skill area 6.5 coverage gaps: treaty-reserved rights, trust responsibility, ISDEAA self-determination/self-governance, Tribal treatment-as-a-state, Tribal law
rationale: Plans require treaty-rights accommodation (102 treaty/reserved-right mentions in 39 plans; e.g., NWFP ACS 'American Indian Uses' restriction test; Nez Perce-Clearwater 2025 FW-DC-TT-09). Fire and forestry run through 638 contracts and compacts. None of this is named in v1. Add TN-C01, TN-C04, TN-C05, TN-C08.

Keep as a competency for non-Tribal professionals: it describes respecting Tribal governance authority over data, which is the project's to describe. Revise per TN-C07 and hold publication until reviewed by a Tribal advisory body (concur with CA needs-evidence). Separately, competencies for Tribal data stewards working inside Tribal governments belong in a Tribally stewarded module, not here.

element: 7.1.1 Expert indicator 'Advises tribal governments on data governance code development'
rationale: Tribes write their own codes. Rewrite: 'At a Tribe's request, provides technical support to Tribally led data governance code development'.

element: 7.1.1 FPIC language ('Designs data governance frameworks that satisfy FPIC standards')
rationale: Legally imprecise. Name the sources of obligation separately: Tribal law (codes, research and data codes); federal policy (DOI did not adopt FPIC for consultation generally, but 301 DM 7 requires FPIC before receiving IK); international standards (UNDRIP). Practitioners need to know which applies.

element: 7.1.1 missing indicator on records law and AI
rationale: Add: 'Explains to Tribal partners, before any data are received, what FOIA and records laws may compel the agency to disclose, without overstating protection' (301 DM 7 s.7.6.A(1)(b)); and 'Prevents ingestion of Tribal data into AI or third-party systems absent Tribal authorization'.

Keep separate from L1 (rights vs distribution is the right distinction). Fix three problems: (1) 'Indigenous peoples and local communities' conflates sovereign Tribal governments (political status) with local communities; (2) treats FPIC as the operative U.S. standard - name Tribal law, federal law/policy and international standards as distinct sources; (3) add trigger conditions for AI ingestion, records disclosure and workforce data about Tribal programs.

element: L2 lens population (4 of 222 competencies tagged; 7.1.4 AI governance L2=A)
rationale: Populate multi-rater with L2 review mandatory for fire (4.2.3, 4.3.x), fisheries (1.4.5), wildlife (1.4.2), water quality (1.2.4), timber planning (1.3.5), AI monitoring (2.6.1, 2.6.2), cultural resources (5.3.3), planning (6.2.x) and AI governance (7.1.4). 7.1.4 L2=A is wrong: AI adoption decisions touch Tribal data; should be at least I. Tagging is analyst work; it does not require Tribal consent, but L2-flagged content goes through the Tribal review gate before publication.

element: Domain 1 Cross-Cutting Competency 4 'Integration of Knowledge Systems'
rationale: Lumps Indigenous knowledge with farmers' and other practitioner knowledge; 301 DM 7 s.7.5 expressly distinguishes IK from local or individual knowledge. 'Finding genuine synthesis' sets a goal that may not be the nation's. Split: practitioner/local knowledge stays (FC lane); IK handled via TN-C10 with holders' authority intact.

element: Domain 2 Cross-Cutting Competency 4 'Ethical and Equitable Technology Practice' (data sovereignty indicators)
rationale: Data-governance protocols 'in partnership with tribal governments' before collection, and CARE alongside FAIR, are sound. Add AI-ingestion and records-disclosure indicators (as 7.1.1).

element: 3.5.5 indicators 'Integrates AI insights with traditional ecological knowledge appropriately' and 'Develops frameworks for integrating AI with Indigenous knowledge respectfully'
rationale: Treats Indigenous knowledge as an input to AI systems. Replace with 'Prevents ingestion of Indigenous knowledge and Tribal confidential information into AI systems without the Tribe's authorization, and supports Tribally governed AI decisions when asked'.

element: Domain 5 career progression 'Cultural Sophistication: From single culture -> cross-cultural -> Indigenous knowledge integration'
rationale: Positions Indigenous knowledge as the top rung of a non-Indigenous professional's skill ladder.

element: Career pathway titles 'Traditional Ecological Knowledge Coordinator' (Expert) and credential 'Membership in or strong relationships with tribal communities often preferred'
rationale: TEK/IK program positions exist inside Tribal governments and are defined by them; agency-side, title the role as Tribal relations or IK liaison with duties set by agreement. 'Membership preferred' should be stated as Indian preference where it lawfully applies (a political classification), as Tribes asked in 2025.

element: Proposed profession family 'Tribal Natural Resource Management'
rationale: Do not create an ethnicity- or jurisdiction-defined family: Tribal foresters are foresters; Tribal water quality specialists are water quality specialists. Represent Tribal employers as a sector actor with role variants that carry the distinct authority, law and accountability (Tribal council, members, treaty obligations), plus a jurisdictional-context facet.

element: v1 fire recommendation to 'institutionalize TEK and Indigenous fire stewardship as professional competencies' and 'co-design credentialed competencies (with Tribes)'
rationale: The project should not credential Indigenous fire stewardship. Tribes already set their own on-reservation qualification standards via compacts. Instead (a) add competencies for non-Tribal staff to support Tribal-led cultural fire under agreements (TN-C06), and (b) reference Tribally defined qualifications only where a Tribe chooses to publish them, under its terms.

Replace a static boolean with dated driver events: EO 14112 rescission (2025-03-14); OMB M-25-36 (2025-10); USWFS stand-up (2026-01/02); Bears Ears Commission eliminated (2026-07); ACHP Part 800 NPRM vote (2026-07-24, pending OIRA). Concur with CA direction.

element: 7.1.2 Intervention authorization (tribal governments among parties with standing)
rationale: Correctly treats Tribal governments as authorities with standing rather than stakeholders.
Keep as Tribal-actor enactment notes in the new sector-actor structure.

element: Fire, fisheries, wildlife, timber and water-quality competencies (4.2.3, 4.3.1-4.3.5, 1.4.5, 1.4.2, 1.3.5, 1.2.4)
rationale: No Tribal enactment notes despite Tribes running these programs and plans requiring treaty-rights accommodation and Tribal access to first foods (e.g., Nez Perce-Clearwater 2025 FW-GDL-TT-02). Add Tribal-actor enactment notes describing the authority context (compact, treaty, Tribal law) - never the content of Tribal knowledge.

element: v1 treatment of Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian contexts
rationale: Absent. ANCSA corporations are consulted under separate DOI policy (512 DM 6/7); Native Hawaiian organizations have a distinct legal status. Sector-actor sub-types and enactment notes must keep these distinct; content requires review by Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian organizations.

Domains mix classifying principles (knowledge tradition D1, technology modality D2, management function D3, field setting D4, communication D5, policy D6, cross-cutting D7) and are collinear with craft (Cramer's V 0.82). Re-derive the top level from durable work functions plus subsector modules; keep v1 domains as a legacy navigation facet and crosswalk.

Skill areas mix disciplines, sectors (3.6 ESG), tool families (2.5 Digital Collaboration Tools; 2.7 Immersive), settings (4.7 Urban infrastructure) and qualification-bound practices (4.3 Fire); 5.6 still carries a '(NEW)' marker. Re-cut by function within subsector modules; move tool-family areas to the tools layer.

element: Fixed five competencies per skill area
v1_location: Data Dictionary 'Future addition protocol' (max 5 per SA); Structure Summary
rationale: An authoring-template artifact, not a content property; it forces lumping and splitting to fit the count. Grain should follow content and job analysis.

element: D.SA.N positional codes used as identifiers
rationale: Positional codes break on any re-cut and cannot carry withdrawn/replaced status. v2 uses opaque persistent IDs; keep the v1 code as an alias and provenance field (NICE Retained/New/Withdrawn pattern).

element: Competency as a single untyped entity
rationale: A 'competency' is variously a knowledge area (1.1.1), tool fluency (2.1.1, 2.5.3), a qualification-gated practice (4.3.2), an administrative function (5.5.2) or a transversal disposition (D7). Type entities (practice capability / knowledge area / transversal practice; tool fluency moves to the tools layer), as ESCO, SFIA, ASC and the Singapore framework do.
v1 convention says 'active-verb phrase', but titles are noun phrases. Use verb+object+context for capability statements and noun phrases only for knowledge concepts.
Useful seed text for 203 of 222. Repair 19 missing descriptions (several merged into the title, e.g. 3.1.1) and strip the '#' markers in 30 D5 rows.

element: Competency content as v2 seed material
rationale: Migrate all 222 as seed records with full provenance; re-derive placement, grain and tags. Do not treat v1 content as validated.

element: Three tasks per competency graded T1-T3 by level
rationale: Fixed count; grading tasks by level conflates work with proficiency; each task is owned by exactly one competency (no many-to-many). Tasks become first-class many-to-many entities with no level grade.

The best-grained v1 content; most statements pass the DACUM task test. Migrate as seed tasks, verify the ~76% inferred D3 text (Pre-Task 15B never run), strip tool and vendor names into the tools layer, and crosswalk to O*NET tasks/DWAs.

element: Task as the unit of exposure analysis
rationale: Correct unit ('jagged' automation inside a competency), consistent with O*NET-anchored exposure research; enables joins to external task-level measures once crosswalked.

element: Four proficiency levels defined by years of experience
rationale: Tenure is not proficiency. Every competency is forced onto all four levels, against the SFIA principle cited in v1's own methodology report. Replace with a generic level-of-responsibility scale plus competency-specific anchors only at the levels where the competency is practiced.

Template text: Foundational-Knowledge begins 'Understands' in 170/192, Advanced-Knowledge 'Expert in' in 189/192 (a level-label collision), Expert-Knowledge 'Shapes' in 189/192. Not observable; IO-led rewrite required.

element: Proficiency indicators (up to six per level)
rationale: Some are good behavioral indicators; many are reputational or latent (Publishes 180, Influences 186, Recognized 52). Carry as draft seeds only; rewrite to observable behaviors with standards; never present as assessment-ready.

v1_location: Proficiency Indicators rows for 5.x.x; Competencies D5 level columns
rationale: Misparsed: Knowledge/Application text sits in the indicator columns with 'Knowledge*:' prefixes; no real indicators exist; the Competencies sheet level columns are empty. Recover from the source text before any reuse.

Categories don't match the charter's 7 sector actors ('Public Agencies' merges federal/state/local/Tribal; Consulting is a business model; Tribal is absent). Free text, 66 rows with stray '*'. Keep as seed illustrations; replace with structured sector-actor role variants and enactment notes.

element: Example positions listed per domain in the source text
rationale: A role inventory exists in v1 prose but was never carried into the database. Recover it as the seed list for the role-profile layer.

element: Domain-level career pathways in the source text
v1_location: Core_V2 'DOMAIN-LEVEL CAREER PATHWAYS' (Entry/Mid/Senior/Expert with skill-area focus)
rationale: Career-lattice data dropped from the database. Recover as seed progression links for CM's career-lattice model.

element: Domain-level cross-cutting competencies in the source text
v1_location: Core_V2 'DOMAIN-LEVEL COMPETENCY FRAMEWORK' blocks (e.g. D4 Safety Consciousness, Physical Fitness; D6 Systems Thinking)
rationale: Transversal and work-style constructs present in the source but absent from the database. Feed them into the transversal practice layer.

Without function-defined role profiles (task bundles with importance and time share, required competencies with level, computed craft blend, sector-actor variants, crosswalks) v1 cannot show how jobs change, compute reskilling gaps or support HR use. The Forester PD prototype had to be hand-built outside the model.
The conceptual core of the theory of change, with clear definitions and an operational test. Use as the rubric for eliciting craft weights.

Collinear with domain (Cramer's V 0.82; domain predicts craft 85.6%; D2 35/35 DC, D4 35/35 FC; FC only in D1 and D4) and cannot represent blends. Several records show craft varying by scale or task (1.1.5, riparian buffer, prescribed fire). Represent as weights on tasks, aggregated into competency and role blend profiles.
Subsumed by task-level craft weights. Keep the v1 value as a provenance field only.

element: Predicted craft distribution used as calibration
rationale: Circular: the prediction was derived from the domain structure and then used to check tags that the domain structure influenced.

element: Integration-point and edge-case documentation for crafts
rationale: High-quality worked cases; reuse as anchor examples in the craft-weight codebook and IO pilot.

v1_location: Structural Conditions report, Scenario taxonomy implications
rationale: Fieldcraft is reproduced by place-based mentorship, Datacraft is more codifiable, Statecraft is tied to legitimacy. Add learning-mode and mentorship-dependence attributes to craft profiles; feeds CLD and curriculum.

A useful information-flow lens (sense, structure, analyze, integrate, decide) for data-to-decision roles, but v1 itself notes it underweights field decisions. Candidate optional facet on work functions; DC and FC to test its value.

Good definitional craft, but the set skews to public lands and conservation and omits water/wastewater utilities, air quality, waste/remediation, EHS/compliance, energy, environmental engineering, public environmental health, parks and labs. Re-derive families as groupings of role profiles by function; carry the boundary text as seed.

element: Core/Supporting tagging of competencies to families
v1_location: Dimension Tags F1-F15; Profession Family View
rationale: A proxy for role requirements: it cannot say which role, at what level or what share of the job. 133/222 competencies have exactly one Core family; 43 have none; maximum is 6. Replace with role-profile requirements (importance and target level) and compute family relevance.
A sound guard against scope creep; reuse in role-profile and competency linking rules.

element: Zero-Core and Foundational Professional Preparation flags
v1_location: Dimension Tags.Zero Core; Foundational Professional Prep
rationale: Defined three inconsistent ways across records and data (~20 zero-Core in Task 9 summary; '7 competencies with Core >=10 families' in chronology; database shows 43 zero-Core, 30 FPP by skill area, max Core count 6). Replace with computed breadth across role profiles; keep the curriculum insight through the transversal layer.

Family-level only; v1 rates 7/15 Low. Several targets look mis-chosen (F11 secondary 25-4031; F13 29-9021; F12 33-1021 labelled 'Fire Inspectors'; F8 23-1011 Lawyers), and 19-2041 Environmental Scientists and Specialists is absent. Rebuild at role and task level with match type, confidence and version. SOC titles not re-verified this session; FH/IA to confirm.

element: F16 Wildland Fire Intelligence family (pending WFIC tasks)
rationale: The function-not-institution principle is right. In v2, fire intelligence should be a role cluster within a fire and emergency function or subsector module, not a new top-level family tag. Use WFIC as a pilot for subsector extension.

element: Acknowledged missing families (marine, Tribal NRM, urban green infrastructure)
v1_location: profession_family_definitions.md 'Profession Families the Taxonomy Does Not Currently Address'
rationale: Marine and coastal become a subsector module; Tribal NRM is a sovereign jurisdictional and sector-actor context, not a family (TN to advise); urban green infrastructure is a cross-family role bundle with its own O&M ladder.

A public-lands project and authorization lifecycle; S1 is primary for 111/222 and S6 for 4. It fits operations, inspection and enforcement, corporate reporting, emergency response and research poorly. Generalize to a subsector-neutral work-function facet on tasks and keep S1-S6 as a named lifecycle profile.
Analytically valuable for permitting reform; keep inside the project and authorization lifecycle profile.
Correct principle; apply it to the generalized work-function facet.

element: Stage tagging caps and dual-primary exceptions
v1_location: Dimension Tags Stage Primary 2 / Secondary 2 / Dual Primary Exception
rationale: Artifacts of competency-level tagging. The database lost the five documented exceptions (Stage Primary 2 and Secondary 2 empty; Dual Primary all False). Stage attaches to tasks in v2.

These are dated, US-federal, reversible events stored as timeless Booleans; 129/222 flagged (58%), so they discriminate poorly; counts are inconsistent (174 vs 184; stale dashboard). Move to the change-signal layer as dated driver events (jurisdiction, instrument, status, direction, source, affected tasks and roles).
A stored summary that drifted; compute on demand.

Fully determined by its rule (100% consistent with reform flags + Ac/S), so it stores no independent judgment; 150/222 are Transition; it omits workforce-reproduction stability. Replace with computed change indicators (direction, velocity, evidence strength, scenario sensitivity, reproduction fragility).
Keep the idea as a lifecycle status on competencies and roles (proposed/emerging/established/declining/withdrawn), with evidence.

element: Exposure instrument as a whole (five dimensions)
v1_location: domain4_task12_working_record.md Section 1; Dimension Tags T13 columns
rationale: Carry the concepts; restructure as dated, attributed assessment records on tasks; codebook re-issue; multi-rater with IRR; external benchmarks. Migrate all v1 values as 'v1 analyst assessment', never as ground truth.

element: Automation type vocabulary incl. Compressive Augmentation (Ac)
rationale: Ac (headcount compression with review-and-certify) is a useful, policy-relevant category; the A/V current-deployment rule and the mode-split flag are good practice. Tighten definitions so descriptive (deployment) and normative (should-not-automate) judgments are separate.

Not independent of automation type: Hi tacit never co-occurs with Ac/S/V (0/277) and Lo tacit with H only once (1/114). Assess it independently as a task attribute and use it as a predictor; or fold it into craft learning-mode attributes.
Valuable concept, but asserted per task with overlapping bands (P 0-5, C 3-8). Derive it from role profiles (which role levels perform the task) once the role layer exists.

element: Automation vector (AI/Ro/Cv) and Cv boundary rule
rationale: The robotics and convergent distinction matters for field work and is rare in AI indices; the Cv operational-inseparability rule is well specified.
Value 3 is never used (0/666); N fuses 'no horizon' with Human-Essential. Replace with dated forecasts with confidence, optionally scenario-conditioned (FS).

v1_location: task13_crossdomain_synthesis.md s7; task14 workbook rules sheet
rationale: Good practice of documented coding rules, but R1 tells coders to expect the FC/DC pattern, and IDs collide (R10 = V-trajectory in the synthesis vs D7 E/A-only elsewhere; the workbook uses D1-1 style). Re-issue as a versioned codebook with unique IDs.
Presented as 'the most robust structural finding', but partly built in by R1 and by overlapping FC and H definitions. Must be re-tested with blind multi-rater coding before any publication.
Stored aggregations hide the jaggedness the instrument exists to show and use drifting vocabularies (N/No/Y/Yes). Compute views from task assessments.
The right instinct (marks session-direct vs reconstructed: 147 vs 75). Expand to full assessment provenance (rater type, method version, model, date, evidence, confidence).

element: Exposure vocabulary drift and counting residuals
v1_location: Dimension Tags CLD Flag/Severity/Modal Contested; synthesis totals

element: Tool, vendor and standard names embedded in competency and task text
rationale: Separate durable capability from tool fluency; move named tools, methods and reporting standards to a fast-moving tools layer linked to tasks. Several references are date-sensitive (DC/PS to confirm current status).

A separately versioned, fast-cadence layer (monthly) for software, instruments, models, reporting frameworks and protocols, linked to tasks. O*NET maintains software skills separately; ASC has a technology tool hierarchy; SFIA keeps tools out of the core.

Dated, sourced evidence events (exposure assessments, posting and PD changes, land management plan requirements from OpenLMP, policy events, O*NET emerging tasks, foresight scenarios) linked to tasks and roles, from which change indicators are computed.

Versioned crosswalk artifacts with match type and confidence to O*NET-SOC tasks/DWAs, ESCO, OPM series and quals, state classes, CIP, credentials and private job architectures. Track upstream releases (O*NET quarterly; ESCO; OPM consolidation through Sep 2027).

element: Persistent IDs, semantic versioning and withdrawn/replaced status
rationale: Adopt the NICE pattern (persistent statement IDs; Retained/New/Withdrawn; major vs minor by backward compatibility), an ESCO-style delta file per release, and multi-format publication.
